New research suggests that powerful currents deep inside the planet slowly raised and lowered entire continents, allowing erosion to erase vast stretches of geological history before they were buried and preserved.
paras.zh: - 科学家们可能终于解释了为什么世界各地的岩石中缺失了长达十亿多年的地球地质历史。新的研究表明，地球深处的强大水流缓慢地抬升和降低了整个大陆，从而使侵蚀作用消除了大片地质历史，然后才将其埋葬和保存下来。

paras.en: More than a billion years of Earth's geological history are missing from some of the planet's rock formations. Scientists have debated the cause of this enormous gap for decades, but new research suggests that the answer may lie in the slow movement of entire continents, driven by powerful forces deep inside Earth.
paras.zh: 地球的一些岩层缺失了超过十亿年的地球地质历史。几十年来，科学家们一直在争论这一巨大差距的原因，但新的研究表明，答案可能在于整个大陆在地球深处强大力量的驱动下缓慢移动。

paras.en: A study led by a PhD candidate at the University of Wollongong (UOW) offers a new explanation for the Great Unconformity, one of geology's most enduring mysteries. Published in the journal Nature, the findings suggest that ancient continents gradually rose and sank over hundreds of millions of years as hot rock moved through Earth's interior. These changes in elevation may have allowed erosion to remove enormous amounts of rock, erasing vast stretches of the planet's geological record.
paras.zh: 卧龙岗大学 (UOW) 的一名博士生领导的一项研究为地质学最持久的谜团之一——大不整合面提供了新的解释。发表在《自然》杂志上的研究结果表明，随着热岩石穿过地球内部，古代大陆在数亿年的时间里逐渐上升和下沉。这些海拔变化可能导致侵蚀去除了大量的岩石，从而抹去了地球上大片的地质记录。

paras.en: Lead author Santosh Dhungana, a UOW PhD candidate, explained that although researchers have proposed numerous explanations for the Great Unconformity, few have been rigorously tested against the long-term behavior of Earth's interior.
paras.zh: 主要作者、伍伦贡大学博士生桑托什·杜加纳 (Santosh Dhungana) 解释说，尽管研究人员对大不整合提出了多种解释，但很少有经过严格的地球内部长期行为测试。

paras.en: "Imagine a book where a huge section in the middle has been ripped out. The Great Unconformity is that gap in Earth's story, with the narrative jumping from the early chapters straight to a much later part of the story. Our research suggests these pages weren't lost by chance," he said.
paras.zh: “想象一下，一本书的中间很大一部分被撕掉了。大不整合是地球故事中的一个空白，叙述从早期章节直接跳到故事的后期部分。我们的研究表明这些页面并不是偶然丢失的，”他说。

paras.en: Earth's Mysterious Missing Billion Years
paras.zh: 地球神秘消失了数十亿年

paras.en: Normally, layers of sedimentary rock accumulate over time, creating a geological timeline in which older rocks lie beneath younger ones. Scientists can study these layers to reconstruct ancient environments and understand how Earth has changed over billions of years.
paras.zh: 通常，沉积岩层会随着时间的推移而积累，形成一条地质时间线，其中较古老的岩石位于较年轻的岩石之下。科学家可以研究这些层来重建古代环境并了解地球在数十亿年来如何变化。

paras.en: Yet this timeline contains a remarkable interruption. At numerous locations worldwide, sedimentary rocks dating to the Cambrian period, around 540 million years ago, rest directly on much older crystalline rocks, including granite that can be more than a billion years old. The intervening geological layers are absent, leaving an enormous break in the record known as the Great Unconformity.
paras.zh: 然而，这个时间线包含了一个显着的中断。在世界各地的许多地方，沉积岩的历史可以追溯到大约 5.4 亿年前的寒武纪，直接沉积在更古老的结晶岩上，包括已有超过 10 亿年历史的花岗岩。中间的地质层不存在，留下了被称为大不整合面的巨大记录。

paras.en: One of the clearest examples is visible in the Grand Canyon in the United States. This region was once part of Laurentia (modern North America), an ancient continental landmass. Similar gaps have been identified in Europe, Australia, Africa and Asia.
paras.zh: 最明显的例子之一是美国大峡谷。该地区曾经是古老大陆劳伦西亚（现代北美）的一部分。欧洲、澳大利亚、非洲和亚洲也存在类似的差距。

paras.en: The amount of missing time varies considerably between locations. In some places, approximately 200 million years of geological history are absent, while elsewhere the gap exceeds a billion years.
paras.zh: 不同地点的缺勤时间差别很大。在一些地方，大约没有2亿年的地质历史，而在其他地方，差距超过10亿年。

paras.en: How Forces Deep Inside Earth May Have Erased the Rock Record
paras.zh: 地球深处的力量如何抹掉岩石记录

paras.en: To investigate what caused these missing chapters, Dhungana worked with his supervisor and co-author, Associate Professor Nicolas Flament, to simulate the movement of Earth's mantle over hundreds of millions of years.
paras.zh: 为了调查导致这些缺失章节的原因，杜加纳与他的导师兼合著者尼古拉斯·弗拉门特副教授合作，模拟了地幔数亿年的运动。

paras.en: The mantle is an immense layer of hot, mostly solid rock beneath Earth's crust. Although this material appears rigid on human timescales, it can deform and flow extremely slowly over geological periods. Heat-driven circulation within the mantle, a process called mantle convection, can gradually raise enormous regions of Earth's surface or cause them to subside.
paras.zh: 地幔是地壳下一层巨大的炽热、大部分为固体的岩石。尽管这种材料在人类时间尺度上看起来是刚性的，但它可以在地质时期内变形并极其缓慢地流动。地幔内由热驱动的循环，这一过程称为地幔对流，可以逐渐抬升地球表面的大片区域或导致它们下沉。

paras.en: These vertical movements can influence whether ancient rocks are exposed to erosion or buried beneath new deposits. When a continent rises, wind, water and other natural processes can gradually wear away its surface. If the land later sinks, oceans can advance over it, allowing fresh sediment to accumulate on top of the eroded rock.
paras.zh: 这些垂直运动会影响古代岩石是否受到侵蚀或埋在新沉积物之下。当大陆上升时，风、水和其他自然过程会逐渐磨损其表面。如果陆地随后下沉，海洋就会淹没它，使新鲜的沉积物积聚在被侵蚀的岩石顶部。

paras.en: The researchers found that this process may explain both the disappearance of ancient rock layers and the preservation of the geological boundary that remains visible today.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，这一过程可以解释古代岩层的消失和至今仍可见的地质边界的保存。

paras.en: Ancient Continents Rose and Sank Over Millions of Years
paras.zh: 古代大陆数百万年来的崛起和沉没

paras.en: The simulations revealed a striking pattern across three major ancient continental regions: Laurentia, Baltica (northern Europe) and North China.
paras.zh: 模拟揭示了三个主要古代大陆地区的惊人模式：劳伦西亚、波罗的海（北欧）和华北。

paras.en: According to the models, mantle convection caused the ancient cores of these continents to rise during the Neoproterozoic Era, which extended from roughly one billion to 540 million years ago. This long interval preceded the Cambrian period, when animal life underwent a remarkable expansion in diversity, commonly known as the Cambrian explosion.
paras.zh: 根据模型，地幔对流导致这些大陆的古老核心在新元古代时期上升，这个时期从大约 10 亿年前延伸到 5.4 亿年前。这个漫长的时期发生在寒武纪之前，当时动物生命的多样性经历了显着的扩张，通常被称为寒武纪大爆发。

paras.en: As the continents remained elevated, prolonged erosion could have stripped away extensive layers of older rock, gradually removing hundreds of millions of years of geological history.
paras.zh: 由于大陆仍然处于升高状态，长期的侵蚀可能会剥去大面积的较古老的岩石，逐渐消除数亿年的地质历史。

paras.en: The researchers found that this period of uplift was followed by widespread subsidence during the Phanerozoic eon, which encompasses approximately the past 540 million years. As these ancient continental regions slowly sank, advancing seas covered their eroded surfaces. New sediments accumulated above the exposed older rocks, preserving the boundary between the two.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，这段抬升时期之后是显生宙期间的广泛下沉，这一时期大约涵盖了过去的 5.4 亿年。随着这些古老的大陆地区慢慢下沉，前进的海洋覆盖了它们被侵蚀的表面。新的沉积物堆积在暴露的旧岩石上方，保留了两者之间的边界。

paras.en: Over immense spans of time, this sequence of uplift, erosion, subsidence and sediment deposition could have produced the Great Unconformity seen in rock formations today.
paras.zh: 在漫长的时间跨度中，这一系列的隆起、侵蚀、沉降和沉积物沉积可能产生了今天岩层中所见的大不整合面。

paras.en: A New Explanation for One of Earth's Greatest Geological Mysteries
paras.zh: 对地球上最大的地质谜团之一的新解释

paras.en: A particularly important finding was how closely the computer simulations matched the geographical distribution of the Great Unconformity.
paras.zh: 一个特别重要的发现是计算机模拟与大不整合面的地理分布的吻合程度。

paras.en: The models predicted long-term uplift followed by subsidence in North America, northern Europe and North China, precisely the regions where the geological gap is especially well documented and preserved.
paras.zh: 这些模型预测了北美、北欧和华北地区的长期隆起和随后的沉降，而这些地区正是地质间隙得到特别详细记录和保存的地区。

paras.en: This agreement provides support for the idea that deep mantle movements played a major role in shaping the missing rock record. Rather than requiring a separate explanation for each location, the findings suggest that a common process operating deep within Earth may account for the widespread pattern.
paras.zh: 该协议支持了深部地幔运动在形成缺失的岩石记录方面发挥了重要作用的观点。研究结果表明，地球深处运行的一个共同过程可能解释了这种广泛的模式，而不是要求对每个位置进行单独的解释。

paras.en: "Sometimes what is missing can tell us more about the story of Earth than what we can see. A single, long period of uplift followed by a long period of sinking would have been the ideal recipe for removing the rock and preserving the worn surface," Associate Professor Flament said.
paras.zh: “有时候，缺失的东西可以告诉我们更多关于地球的故事，而不是我们所看到的。弗拉门特副教授说，一次长期的隆起，然后是长期的下沉，可能是去除岩石和保留磨损表面的理想方法。”

paras.en: The research offers a way to connect the geological evidence visible at Earth's surface with the slow processes occurring far below it. Although the findings do not establish that mantle convection was the only factor responsible for the Great Unconformity, they provide a testable explanation for why so much ancient geological history disappeared and how the remaining evidence survived.
paras.zh: 这项研究提供了一种将地球表面可见的地质证据与远低于地球的缓慢过程联系起来的方法。尽管这些发现并没有证明地幔对流是造成大不整合的唯一因素，但它们为为什么如此多的古代地质历史消失以及剩余的证据如何幸存提供了可检验的解释。

paras.en: "Many explanations for the Great Unconformity had been proposed but few had been tested against how the Earth actually behaves over time. It is a thrill to be able to propose a solution to this geological puzzle."
paras.zh: “人们对大不整合面提出了许多解释，但很少有人根据地球随时间的实际变化进行测试。能够为这个地质难题提出解决方案真是令人兴奋。”

paras.zh: 材料由卧龙岗大学提供。注意：内容的风格和长度可能会被编辑。

articles.title: A little-known protein could be a powerful weapon against Alzheimer’s

paras.en: A little-known protein could be a powerful weapon against Alzheimerâs
paras.zh: 一种鲜为人知的蛋白质可能是对抗阿尔茨海默病的有力武器

paras.en: - Scientists have uncovered a powerful natural defense against Alzheimerâs disease that could open the door to new treatments. By boosting a protein called SORLA, researchers significantly reduced toxic tau tangles, protected connections between brain cells, and prevented some of the brain shrinkage associated with neurodegeneration in mice. Removing the protein made the damage worse, highlighting its critical protective role.
paras.zh: - 科学家们发现了一种针对阿尔茨海默病的强大天然防御机制，这可能为新疗法打开大门。通过增强一种名为 SORLA 的蛋白质，研究人员显着减少了有毒的 tau 蛋白缠结，保护了脑细胞之间的连接，并防止了与小鼠神经退行性疾病相关的一些大脑萎缩。去除蛋白质会使损伤更加严重，凸显了其至关重要的保护作用。

paras.en: A protein that helps protect the brain may offer scientists a promising new way to fight Alzheimer's disease and other forms of dementia. Researchers have discovered that increasing levels of this protein can reduce the buildup of toxic tangles associated with brain damage, while also helping preserve the connections that allow nerve cells to communicate.
paras.zh: 一种有助于保护大脑的蛋白质可能为科学家提供一种有希望的新方法来对抗阿尔茨海默病和其他形式的痴呆症。研究人员发现，增加这种蛋白质的水平可以减少与脑损伤相关的有毒缠结的积累，同时还有助于保护神经细胞进行交流的连接。

paras.en: The findings, published in Science Advances by scientists at Sanford Burnham Prebys, suggest that strengthening the brain's own protective mechanisms could eventually lead to new treatments for neurodegenerative diseases. In experiments with mice, the researchers found that boosting the protein reduced several damaging changes associated with Alzheimer's, including brain shrinkage and the accumulation of abnormal tau proteins.
paras.zh: 桑福德伯纳姆普雷比学院的科学家在《科学进展》上发表的研究结果表明，加强大脑自身的保护机制最终可能会带来神经退行性疾病的新疗法。在小鼠实验中，研究人员发现，增加这种蛋白质的含量可以减少与阿尔茨海默氏症相关的几种破坏性变化，包括大脑萎缩和异常 tau 蛋白的积累。

paras.en: The discovery is particularly significant because tau plays an essential role in keeping healthy brain cells functioning. Under normal conditions, tau proteins help stabilize microtubules, tiny structures that provide internal support to neurons and help maintain the intricate networks of the nervous system.
paras.zh: 这一发现尤为重要，因为 tau 蛋白在保持健康脑细胞功能方面发挥着重要作用。在正常情况下，tau 蛋白有助于稳定微管，这种微小结构为神经元提供内部支持，并有助于维持神经系统的复杂网络。

paras.en: In Alzheimer's and several related disorders, however, tau proteins can become abnormal and stick together, forming harmful clumps known as tau tangles. These tangles disrupt the normal functioning of nerve cells and are associated with cognitive decline and neuronal death. Diseases characterized by abnormal tau accumulation are collectively called tauopathies.
paras.zh: 然而，在阿尔茨海默氏症和几种相关疾病中，tau 蛋白可能变得异常并粘在一起，形成称为 tau 缠结的有害团块。这些缠结会破坏神经细胞的正常功能，并与认知能力下降和神经元死亡有关。以 tau 蛋白异常积累为特征的疾病统称为 tau 病。

paras.en: A Protective Protein With a Surprising Role in Alzheimer's
paras.zh: 一种在阿尔茨海默病中具有惊人作用的保护性蛋白质

paras.en: The researchers investigated a protein called sorting-related receptor with A-type repeats (SORLA), which has already attracted scientific attention for its potential role in protecting the brain against Alzheimer's disease.
paras.zh: 研究人员研究了一种名为 A 型重复分选相关受体 (SORLA) 的蛋白质，该蛋白质因其在保护大脑免受阿尔茨海默病的潜在作用而引起了科学界的关注。

paras.en: Previous studies have shown that SORLA can help limit the production and accumulation of amyloid-beta, another protein closely associated with Alzheimer's. Amyloid-beta can build up into plaques in the brain, making it one of the disease's major pathological hallmarks alongside tau tangles.
paras.zh: 先前的研究表明，SORLA 可以帮助限制β-淀粉样蛋白的产生和积累，β-淀粉样蛋白是另一种与阿尔茨海默病密切相关的蛋白质。 β 淀粉样蛋白可以在大脑中积聚成斑块，使其与 tau 蛋白缠结一起成为该疾病的主要病理特征之一。

paras.en: "In the last 15 or 20 years, considerable data has come out from our lab and other groups showing that SORLA can suppress one of the hallmarks of Alzheimer's disease -- amyloid-beta generation and accumulation," said Timothy Huang, PhD, assistant professor in the Center for Neurologic Diseases at Sanford Burnham Prebys.
paras.zh: “在过去的 15 或 20 年里，我们的实验室和其他小组得出的大量数据表明，SORLA 可以抑制阿尔茨海默病的标志之一——β-淀粉样蛋白的生成和积累，”桑福德伯纳姆普雷比学院神经系统疾病中心助理教授 Timothy Huang 博士说。

paras.en: "Very little was known, however, about whether SORLA affected the tau tangles reflected on the other side of the coin in Alzheimer's disease."
paras.zh: “然而，人们对 SORLA 是否影响阿尔茨海默病中硬币另一面的 tau 蛋白缠结影响知之甚少。”

paras.en: To investigate this question, the scientists developed a mouse model by breeding animals engineered to produce additional human SORLA with mice that develop tau tangles, brain atrophy, and cognitive impairments. This allowed them to examine whether higher SORLA levels could reduce tau accumulation and protect against the damage it causes.
paras.zh: 为了研究这个问题，科学家们开发了一种小鼠模型，将能够产生额外人类 SORLA 的动物与出现 tau 蛋白缠结、脑萎缩和认知障碍的小鼠进行繁殖。这使他们能够检查较高的 SORLA 水平是否可以减少 tau 积累并防止其造成的损害。

paras.en: Boosting SORLA Reduces Toxic Tau and Brain Shrinkage
paras.zh: 增强 SORLA 可减少有毒 Tau 蛋白和大脑萎缩

paras.en: The results revealed that additional SORLA provided protection against several processes that contribute to tau tangles and the progression of neurodegenerative disease.
paras.zh: 结果表明，额外的 SORLA 可以针对导致 tau 缠结和神经退行性疾病进展的多种过程提供保护。

paras.en: One important effect involved a process called hyperphosphorylation. This occurs when too many phosphate groups attach to tau proteins, altering their behavior and contributing to the development of harmful tangles. Higher SORLA levels reduced this abnormal modification.
paras.zh: 一个重要的影响涉及一种称为过度磷酸化的过程。当太多磷酸基团附着在 tau 蛋白上时，就会发生这种情况，改变它们的行为并导致有害缠结的发展。较高的 SORLA 水平减少了这种异常修饰。

paras.en: The protein also limited the ability of misfolded tau to act as "seeds" that encourage other tau proteins to clump together. This seeding process can help toxic tau aggregates multiply and spread their damaging effects.
paras.zh: 该蛋白还限制了错误折叠的 tau 蛋白作为“种子”的能力，从而鼓励其他 tau 蛋白聚集在一起。这种播种过程可以帮助有毒的 tau 蛋白聚集体繁殖并传播其破坏性影响。

paras.en: Beyond reducing tau abnormalities, SORLA helped preserve synapses, the specialized connections through which neurons communicate. It also protected synaptic plasticity, the brain's ability to strengthen or modify those connections, which is essential for learning, memory, and normal cognitive function.
paras.zh: 除了减少 tau 蛋白异常之外，SORLA 还有助于保护突触，即神经元进行交流的特殊连接。它还保护突触可塑性，即大脑加强或修改这些连接的能力，这对于学习、记忆和正常认知功能至关重要。

paras.en: "When you upregulate SORLA, you can suppress the negative effects found in tauopathies," said Huijie Huang, PhD, a staff scientist in the Huang lab at Sanford Burnham Prebys and lead author of the study.
paras.zh: “当你上调 SORLA 时，你可以抑制 tau蛋白病中发现的负面影响，”桑福德伯纳姆普雷比斯大学黄实验室的研究员、该研究的主要作者 Huijie Huang 博士说。

paras.en: "We found there was less brain atrophy and less tau accumulation, which was very exciting to see."
paras.zh: “我们发现脑萎缩和 tau 蛋白积累减少，这是非常令人兴奋的。”

paras.en: Removing the Protein Makes Brain Damage Worse
paras.zh: 去除蛋白质会使大脑损伤更加严重

paras.en: After observing the benefits of increasing SORLA, the researchers examined what would happen if the protein were missing entirely.
paras.zh: 在观察到增加 SORLA 的好处后，研究人员研究了如果该蛋白质完全缺失会发生什么。

paras.en: SORLA is produced using instructions encoded by a gene called Sorl1. Some people carry mutations that interfere with this gene's function, potentially disrupting the production or activity of the protective protein.
paras.zh: SORLA 是使用 Sorl1 基因编码的指令产生的。有些人携带的突变会干扰该基因的功能，可能会破坏保护性蛋白质的产生或活性。

paras.en: To investigate the consequences, the team studied genetically modified mice that lacked Sorl1 and therefore could not produce SORLA.
paras.zh: 为了研究其后果，研究小组研究了缺乏 Sorl1 并因此无法产生 SORLA 的转基因小鼠。

paras.en: The results contrasted sharply with those seen in mice carrying additional copies of the protein. Instead of protecting against tau-related damage, the absence of SORLA made the harmful effects more severe.
paras.zh: 结果与携带额外蛋白质拷贝的小鼠中观察到的结果形成鲜明对比。 SORLA 的缺失不但不能防止 tau 相关损伤，反而使有害影响更加严重。

paras.en: "The opposite turned out to be true when we deleted the ability to produce SORLA proteins," said Tim Huang, senior and corresponding author of the manuscript. "A lack of SORLA exacerbated the harmful effects observed in tauopathies."
paras.zh: 该手稿的资深通讯作者蒂姆·黄 (Tim Huang) 说：“当我们删除了产生 SORLA 蛋白的能力时，结果恰恰相反。” “缺乏 SORLA 会加剧在 tau 蛋白病中观察到的有害影响。”

paras.en: These contrasting results provided further evidence that SORLA plays an important protective role in the brain and may influence how severely tau-related diseases progress.
paras.zh: 这些对比结果进一步证明 SORLA 在大脑中发挥着重要的保护作用，并可能影响 tau 相关疾病进展的严重程度。

paras.en: A New Clue Could Lead to Alzheimer's Treatments
paras.zh: 一条新线索可能导致阿尔茨海默氏症的治疗

paras.en: To understand why changing SORLA levels had such different effects, the researchers examined the molecular activity of individual brain cells and the surrounding tissue.
paras.zh: 为了了解为什么改变 SORLA 水平会产生如此不同的影响，研究人员检查了单个脑细胞和周围组织的分子活动。

paras.en: They combined advanced sequencing methods to measure protein levels and gene activity in individual cells with techniques that map where RNA and proteins are located within brain tissue. This detailed approach helped reveal how SORLA influences the biological processes involved in neurodegeneration.
paras.zh: 他们将先进的测序方法与绘制 RNA 和蛋白质在脑组织内位置的技术相结合，测量单个细胞中的蛋白质水平和基因活性。这种详细的方法有助于揭示 SORLA 如何影响神经退行性病变的生物过程。

paras.en: The analysis showed that increasing SORLA helped prevent harmful changes in protein production at synapses while also suppressing other mechanisms associated with tauopathy progression.
paras.zh: 分析表明，增加 SORLA 有助于防止突触蛋白质产生的有害变化，同时还抑制与 tau 蛋白病进展相关的其他机制。

paras.en: The researchers also discovered that higher SORLA levels reduced abnormal gene activity in glial cells. These cells perform several essential functions in the nervous system, including supporting, maintaining, and protecting neurons. Changes in glial cell activity can contribute to the progression of neurodegenerative diseases.
paras.zh: 研究人员还发现，较高的 SORLA 水平可以减少神经胶质细胞中的异常基因活性。这些细胞在神经系统中执行多种基本功能，包括支持、维持和保护神经元。神经胶质细胞活性的变化可能导致神经退行性疾病的进展。

paras.en: One finding was especially intriguing because it pointed toward a potential target for existing medications.
paras.zh: 一项发现特别有趣，因为它指出了现有药物的潜在目标。

paras.en: "One particularly notable finding that we can build on is the upregulation of a member of the plexin-B family of receptors in the absence of SORLA," said Huijie Huang.
paras.zh: “我们可以借鉴的一个特别值得注意的发现是，在没有 SORLA 的情况下，plexin-B 受体家族成员的上调，”Huijie Huang 说。

paras.en: Plexin-B receptors are proteins involved in cellular signaling, helping cells respond to information from their surroundings. The increased activity of a receptor in this family when SORLA was absent suggests that this signaling pathway could be involved in some of the damaging changes associated with tau disorders.
paras.zh: Plexin-B 受体是参与细胞信号传导的蛋白质，帮助细胞对周围环境的信息做出反应。当 SORLA 缺失时，该家族中受体的活性增加表明该信号通路可能参与了与 tau 蛋白紊乱相关的一些破坏性变化。

paras.en: Importantly, drugs capable of targeting this family of receptors already exist, raising the possibility that scientists could investigate whether they might be useful against tau-related dementia.
paras.zh: 重要的是，能够靶向该受体家族的药物已经存在，这增加了科学家研究它们是否可用于治疗 tau 相关痴呆的可能性。

paras.en: "There are unique drugs that can target this class of receptors that we may be able to apply to tau-related dementia disorders," said Tim Huang. "One potential future direction is to repurpose these drugs to target overactivation of glial cells and perhaps reverse some of the phenotypes in tauopathies."
paras.zh: Tim Huang 说：“有一些独特的药物可以针对此类受体，我们或许可以将其应用于与 tau 相关的痴呆症。” “未来一个潜在的方向是重新调整这些药物的用途，以靶向神经胶质细胞的过度激活，并可能逆转 tau蛋白病的一些表型。”

paras.en: The Next Step Toward Human Alzheimer's Research
paras.zh: 人类阿尔茨海默病研究的下一步

paras.en: Although the findings are encouraging, the protective effects were demonstrated in mice, and more research is needed to determine how these mechanisms operate in humans.
paras.zh: 尽管这些发现令人鼓舞，但保护作用已在小鼠身上得到证实，还需要更多的研究来确定这些机制如何在人体中发挥作用。

paras.en: The team now hopes to investigate how individual types of brain cells respond when SORLA levels increase or decrease. One planned approach involves transplanting human neurons or glial cells into mouse brains, allowing researchers to examine the effects of different SORLA mutations in a living brain affected by disease.
paras.zh: 该团队现在希望研究当 SORLA 水平升高或降低时，不同类型的脑细胞有何反应。一种计划中的方法是将人类神经元或神经胶质细胞移植到小鼠大脑中，使研究人员能够检查不同 SORLA 突变对受疾病影响的活体大脑的影响。

paras.en: "Mouse cells and human cells are different," said Tim Huang. "Because we're looking at human disease, it's more informative if we can observe the modulation and dysfunction of SORLA in the context of a human cell inside of a diseased brain environment."
paras.zh: “小鼠细胞和人类细胞是不同的，”蒂姆·黄说。 “因为我们正在研究人类疾病，所以如果我们能够在患病大脑环境内的人类细胞中观察 SORLA 的调节和功能障碍，就会提供更多信息。”

paras.en: These experiments could help clarify how SORLA protects neurons from toxic tau accumulation and why disruptions in its function make neurodegeneration worse.
paras.zh: 这些实验可以帮助阐明 SORLA 如何保护神经元免受有毒 tau 蛋白积累的影响，以及为什么其功能的破坏会导致神经退行性恶化。

paras.en: Ultimately, the researchers hope that a deeper understanding of this protective protein will reveal new treatment strategies, either by enhancing SORLA's activity or by repurposing existing drugs to interfere with damaging cellular pathways. Such approaches could eventually offer new ways to combat Alzheimer's disease and other forms of dementia driven by toxic tau tangles.
paras.zh: 最终，研究人员希望对这种保护性蛋白的更深入了解将揭示新的治疗策略，要么通过增强 SORLA 的活性，要么通过重新利用现有药物来干扰破坏性细胞途径。这些方法最终可能会提供新的方法来对抗阿尔茨海默病和由有毒 tau 蛋白缠结引起的其他形式的痴呆症。

paras.en: The study was supported by the National Institutes of Health, National Cancer Institute and National Institute on Aging.
paras.zh: 该研究得到了美国国立卫生研究院、美国国家癌症研究所和美国国家老龄化研究所的支持。

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 18, 2013: NASA launches MAVEN spacecraft to Mars to find out how the Red Planet lost its water
articles.author: Hanneke Weitering

paras.en: On Nov. 18, 2013, NASA launched the MAVEN spacecraft to Mars.
paras.zh: 2013年11月18日，美国宇航局向火星发射了MAVEN航天器。

paras.en: The name of NASA's MAVEN spacecraft stands for Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN. The spacecraft was an orbiter designed to help scientists figure out what happened to the water on Mars and its atmosphere. Mars is dry today, but it data from several Mars missions suggest that it was a much wetter environment a long time ago.
paras.zh: NASA 的 MAVEN 航天器的名称代表火星大气和挥发性演化。该航天器是一个轨道飞行器，旨在帮助科学家弄清楚火星上的水及其大气发生了什么。今天的火星很干燥，但来自几次火星任务的数据表明，很久以前火星的环境要湿润得多。

paras.en: MAVEN tracked the rate of atmospheric loss from Mars. The planet has a super thin atmosphere that has been leaking into space for a few billion years. Scientists think that when Mars lost its atmosphere, water dried up on the surface as a result.
paras.zh: MAVEN 追踪了火星大气层损失的速度。这颗行星拥有超稀薄的大气层，数十亿年来一直在泄漏到太空中。科学家认为，当火星失去大气层时，表面的水就会干涸。

paras.en: Solar storms that blast radiation into the solar system appear to have blasted away some of the atmosphere. Carbon dioxide in the atmosphere once kept Mars warm enough to sustain liquid water on its surface, and losing that greenhouse gas turned Mars into a cold and dry place.
paras.zh: 将辐射喷射到太阳系的太阳风暴似乎已经吹走了一些大气层。大气中的二氧化碳曾经使火星足够温暖，足以维持其表面的液态水，失去温室气体使火星变成一个寒冷干燥的地方。

paras.en: NASA's MAVEN spacecraft was the first Mars orbiter ever built to measure how the Martian atmosphere interacts with solar wind, as well as how that constant stream of particles from the sun slowly stripped the Red Planet of its precious atmosphere over time.
paras.zh: NASA 的 MAVEN 航天器是有史以来建造的第一个火星轨道飞行器，用于测量火星大气层如何与太阳风相互作用，以及来自太阳的持续粒子流如何随着时间的推移慢慢地剥夺这颗红色星球上珍贵的大气层。

paras.en: After its launch in 2013, MAVEN spent about 10 months en route to Mars before entering orbit on Sept. 21, 2014. The spacecraft then spent the better part of 11 years studying the Red Planet from orbit using three different suites of instruments: An imaging ultraviolet spectrograph to study the global characteristics of the Martian atmosphere; a Neutral Gas and Ion Mass Spectromenter to measure its composition; and a six-instrument setup to study how Mars' ionosphere reacts to solar wind.
paras.zh: 2013 年发射后，MAVEN 在飞往火星的途中花了大约 10 个月的时间，然后于 2014 年 9 月 21 日进入轨道。随后，这艘航天器花了 11 年的大部分时间，使用三套不同的仪器在轨道上研究这颗红色星球：成像紫外光谱仪，用于研究火星大气的整体特征；用于测量其成分的中性气体和离子质谱仪；以及一个由六台仪器组成的装置，用于研究火星电离层对太阳风的反应。

paras.en: "The science MAVEN has given us is key to informing what kind of radiation protection and safety measures we must take before sending humans to Mars," Louise Prockter, NASA director of planetary science, said in June 2026 after the mission concluded. "The data collected from MAVEN will continue to provide valuable insight into Mars for decades to come."
paras.zh: NASA 行星科学主任路易斯·普罗克特 (Louise Prockter) 于 2026 年 6 月任务结束后表示：“MAVEN 为我们提供的科学知识对于我们了解在将人类送上火星之前必须采取何种辐射防护和安全措施至关重要。” “从 MAVEN 收集的数据将在未来几十年继续提供对火星的宝贵见解。”

paras.en: MAVEN was originally designed to study Mars for 1 full Earth year after arriving at the Red Planet. That mission ended in 2016, but the spacecraft managed to survive for another 10 years adding more observations for scientists to study.
paras.zh: MAVEN 最初的设计目的是在到达火星后用 1 个地球年来研究火星。该任务于 2016 年结束，但航天器又存活了 10 年，为科学家提供了更多观测结果供研究。

paras.en: NASA ultimately began using MAVEN as a communications relay for other missions at Mars as the orbiter aged. In December 2025, MAVEN went silent, with NASA losing communication with the orbiter.
paras.zh: 随着轨道器老化，NASA 最终开始使用 MAVEN 作为火星其他任务的通信中继。 2025 年 12 月，MAVEN 陷入沉寂，美国宇航局与轨道器失去了联系。

paras.en: An investigation later found that the probe sent its final signal on Dec. 6, 2025 as it was heading behind Mars (as seen from Earth). But when it emerged on the other side, it had gone into an uncontrollable spin that led to a loss of power, dooming the spacecraft.
paras.zh: 后来的一项调查发现，探测器于 2025 年 12 月 6 日发出了最终信号，当时它正驶向火星后方（从地球上看）。但当它出现在另一边时，它陷入了无法控制的旋转，导致动力丧失，导致航天器灭亡。

paras.en: NASA tried in vain to recover the spacecraft over several months, ultimately declaring the mission over in June 2026.
paras.zh: 美国宇航局 (NASA) 花了几个月的时间试图回收这艘航天器，但没有成功，最终于 2026 年 6 月宣布任务结束。

paras.en: "Best. Mars. Mission. Ever," Shannon Curry, MAVEN's principal investigator, said of the probe entire 12.5-year mission when it ended. The team "really experienced the loss of a loved one with the end of the mission here."
paras.zh: MAVEN 的首席研究员香农·库里 (Shannon Curry) 在谈到探测器结束时整个 12.5 年的任务时说：“有史以来最好的火星任务。”该团队“随着任务的结束，真正经历了失去亲人的痛苦”。

paras.en: Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube.
paras.zh: 想要更多太空历史吗？查看我们完整的“太空中的这一天”故事存档，并在 YouTube 上观看“太空中的这一天”视频。

paras.en: Hanneke Weitering is a multimedia journalist in the Pacific Northwest reporting on the future of aviation at FutureFlight.aero and Aviation International News and was previously the Editor for Spaceflight and Astronomy news here at Space.com. As an editor with over 10 years of experience in science journalism she has previously written for Scholastic Classroom Magazines, MedPage Today and The Joint Institute for Computational Sciences at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. After studying physics at the University of Tennessee in her hometown of Knoxville, she earned her graduate degree in Science, Health and Environmental Reporting (SHERP) from New York University. Hanneke joined the Space.com team in 2016 as a staff writer and producer, covering topics including spaceflight and astronomy. She currently lives in Seattle, home of the Space Needle, with her cat and two snakes. In her spare time, Hanneke enjoys exploring the Rocky Mountains, basking in nature and looking for dark skies to gaze at the cosmos.
paras.zh: Hanneke Weitering 是西北太平洋地区的一名多媒体记者，在 FutureFlight.aero 和 Aviation International News 报道航空业的未来，此前曾担任 Space.com 的航天和天文学新闻编辑。作为一名拥有 10 多年科学新闻经验的编辑，她曾为学术课堂杂志、MedPage Today 和橡树岭国家实验室计算科学研究所撰写文章。在家乡诺克斯维尔的田纳西大学学习物理学后，她在纽约大学获得了科学、健康和环境报告 (SHERP) 研究生学位。 Hanneke 于 2016 年加入 Space.com 团队，担任专职撰稿人和制作人，涵盖航天和天文学等主题。她目前与她的猫和两条蛇住在太空针塔所在地西雅图。在业余时间，汉内克喜欢探索落基山脉，沐浴在大自然中，寻找黑暗的天空凝视宇宙。

articles.title: Astronomers witness a star eating its companion in 1st-of-its-kind observation
articles.author: Charles Q. Choi

paras.en: Astronomers may have, for the first time ever, directly witnessed a star engulfing its companion, a new study reports.
paras.zh: 一项新的研究报告称，天文学家可能有史以来第一次直接目睹一颗恒星吞噬其伴星。

paras.en: As stars die, they swell up to hundreds of times their original size, consuming anything orbiting nearby. In a binary star system, this can include a dying star merging with its companion star. However, scientists had never directly seen any examples of such a cosmic drama unfolding — until now.
paras.zh: 当恒星死亡时，它们会膨胀到原来大小的数百倍，吞噬附近绕轨道运行的任何东西。在双星系统中，这可能包括垂死的恒星与其伴星合并。然而，直到现在，科学家们还从未直接看到过此类宇宙戏剧上演的任何例子。

paras.en: "Catching a star engulfing its companion in the act is very difficult," study lead author Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University in New York, told Space.com. "When a star engulfs its companion, its effect is very subtle — like throwing a bucket of water in a large ocean. We need sensitive telescopes monitoring the sky for a long time in order to catch this effect."
paras.zh: 研究报告的主要作者、纽约哥伦比亚大学的天体物理学家维拉吉·卡拉姆贝尔卡 (Viraj Karambelkar) 告诉 Space.com：“捕捉到一颗恒星吞噬其伴星的过程非常困难。” “当一颗恒星吞没它的伴星时，它的影响是非常微妙的——就像把一桶水扔进大海一样。我们需要灵敏的望远镜长时间监测天空，才能捕捉到这种效应。”

paras.en: In the new study, the researchers investigated a red giant star designated WNTR23bzdiq, which is located about 2.5 million light-years away in the Andromeda galaxy. The star is about seven times heftier and 350 times wider than our own sun.
paras.zh: 在这项新研究中，研究人员调查了一颗名为 WNTR23bzdiq 的红巨星，它位于仙女座星系中，距离我们约 250 万光年。这颗恒星的重量约为太阳的 7 倍，宽度约为太阳的 350 倍。

paras.en: In 2023, using NASA's now-defunct NEOWISE space telescope and the WINTER telescope at Palomar Observatory in California, the scientists noticed that this star was brightening. By analyzing previous records, they found that the red giant had gradually started growing more luminous in 2018.
paras.zh: 2023 年，科学家们利用美国宇航局现已废弃的 NEOWISE 太空望远镜和加州帕洛玛天文台的 WINTER 望远镜，注意到这颗恒星正在变亮。通过分析之前的记录，他们发现红巨星在2018年开始逐渐变得更加明亮。

paras.en: The researchers had previously suggested this brightening potentially occurred because the giant star engulfed a companion star. As this companion spiraled toward the giant's core, it would generate friction, heat and light, explaining the increasing luminosity.
paras.zh: 研究人员此前曾表示，这种增亮可能是由于这颗巨星吞没了一颗伴星而发生的。当这个伴星盘旋飞向巨人的核心时，它会产生摩擦、热量和光，这解释了亮度增加的原因。

paras.en: Then, near the end of 2025, the astronomers saw a giant eruption of light from this giant star. NASA's James Webb Space Telescope observed the star just 47 days after that eruption, allowing the team to characterize the event in detail. The researchers now propose that this explosion happened when a companion star about 70% the sun's mass rammed into the giant's heart.
paras.zh: 然后，在 2025 年底附近，天文学家看到这颗巨星爆发了巨大的光芒。 NASA 的詹姆斯·韦伯太空望远镜在喷发后仅 47 天就观测到了这颗恒星，使研究小组能够详细描述该事件的特征。研究人员现在提出，这次爆炸是在一颗质量约为太阳 70% 的伴星撞击这颗巨星的心脏时发生的。

paras.en: "I was absolutely flabbergasted when we saw this," Karambelkar said.
paras.zh: “当我们看到这个时，我完全惊呆了，”卡拉姆贝尔卡说。

paras.en: In the new study, the scientists estimated that the eruption expelled an amount of material equal to about 0.1 to 0.2 times the mass of the sun. "Stars engulfing their companions have been theorized for many decades, and this event provides the first observations of this theoretical prediction," Karambelkar said.
paras.zh: 在这项新研究中，科学家们估计这次喷发喷出的物质数量约为太阳质量的0.1至0.2倍。卡拉姆贝尔卡说：“数十年来，恒星吞噬其同伴的理论一直存在，而这一事件提供了对这一理论预测的首次观察。”

paras.en: Although these findings suggest that two stars — a binary system nicknamed "Bao" — merged into one, "it is not the only possibility," Karambelkar said. "The other possibility is that both stars survived, in a much shorter orbit. In order to conclusively determine what happened, we need to continue monitoring what the system does, once the heft of the eruption settles down."
paras.zh: 卡拉姆贝尔卡说，尽管这些发现表明两颗恒星——一个绰号为“包”的双星系统——合并为一颗，“这并不是唯一的可能性”。 “另一种可能性是，两颗恒星都在更短的轨道上幸存下来。为了最终确定发生了什么，一旦喷发的强度稳定下来，我们需要继续监测系统的作用。”

paras.en: Now that astronomers may have found the first such merger, "I can't wait to find more," Karambelkar said. "Upcoming telescopes like the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope and the Vera Rubin Observatory will be very useful in discovering many more such events."
paras.zh: 现在天文学家可能已经发现了第一个此类合并，“我迫不及待地想找到更多，”卡拉姆贝尔卡说。 “即将推出的望远镜，如南希·格雷斯·罗马太空望远镜和维拉·鲁宾天文台，对于发现更多此类事件将非常有用。”

paras.en: The scientists detailed their findings Nov. 18 in the journal Nature.
paras.zh: 科学家们于 11 月 18 日在《自然》杂志上详细介绍了他们的发现。

paras.en: Charles Q. Choi is a contributing writer for Space.com and Live Science. He covers all things human origins and astronomy as well as physics, animals and general science topics. Charles has a Master of Arts degree from the University of Missouri-Columbia, School of Journalism and a Bachelor of Arts degree from the University of South Florida. Charles has visited every continent on Earth, drinking rancid yak butter tea in Lhasa, snorkeling with sea lions in the Galapagos and even climbing an iceberg in Antarctica. Visit him at http://www.sciwriter.us
paras.zh: Charles Q. Choi 是 Space.com 和 Live Science 的特约撰稿人。他涵盖了人类起源和天文学以及物理学、动物和一般科学主题的所有内容。 Charles 拥有密苏里大学哥伦比亚分校新闻学院文学硕士学位和南佛罗里达大学文学学士学位。查尔斯去过地球上的每一个大陆，在拉萨喝腐臭的酥油茶，在加拉帕戈斯群岛与海狮一起浮潜，甚至在南极洲攀登冰山。请访问他：http://www.sciwriter.us

paras.en: Harry joined Space.com in December 2024 as an e-commerce staff writer covering cameras, optics, and skywatching content. Based in the UK, Harry graduated in 2019 with a Bachelor's degree in American Literature with Creative Writing from the University of East Anglia. A keen photographer, Harry has strong experience with astrophotography and has captured celestial objects with a range of cameras. As a lifelong skywatcher, Harry remembers watching the Perseid meteor shower every summer in his hometown and being amazed by the wonders of the night sky.
paras.zh: Harry 于 2024 年 12 月加入 Space.com，担任电子商务特约撰稿人，涵盖相机、光学和观天内容。 Harry 居住在英国，于 2019 年毕业于东安格利亚大学，获得美国文学与创意写作学士学位。哈利是一位敏锐的摄影师，在天文摄影方面拥有丰富的经验，并使用各种相机捕捉到天体。作为一名终生的天文观察者，哈利记得每年夏天都会在家乡观看英仙座流星雨，并对夜空的奇观感到惊叹。

articles.title: UARX Space Marks a Milestone for Spain’s Space Industry with the Maiden Flight of OSSIE-D, Featuring a Complete Power Subsystem Supplied by DHV Technology
articles.author: UARX Space

paras.en: Nigrán, Spain | November 12 2026 – UARX Space has achieved a major milestone for Spain’s space industry with the deployment of OSSIE-D, an Orbital Transfer Vehicle (OTV) designed and manufactured entirely in Spain, with 75% of its components developed in-house by the company. Launched aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, OSSIE-D was deployed using SAU&RON 24, UARX Space’s proprietary separation system. The achievement marks a world first, bringing together an orbital transfer vehicle and a separation system developed by the same company in a single mission.
paras.zh: 西班牙尼格兰| 2026 年 11 月 12 日 – UARX Space 部署了 OSSIE-D，实现了西班牙航天工业的一个重要里程碑。OSSIE-D 是一种完全在西班牙设计和制造的轨道传输飞行器 (OTV)，其 75% 的组件由该公司内部开发。 OSSIE-D 由 SpaceX Falcon 9 火箭发射，并使用 UARX Space 的专有分离系统 SAU&RON 24 进行部署。这一成就标志着世界首创，将同一家公司开发的轨道传输飞行器和分离系统结合在一次任务中。

paras.en: The mission represents a significant advance in Spain’s space technology capabilities, demonstrating the ability to develop and integrate key technologies for in-space transportation and orbital operations. By combining its OTV with its own SAU&RON 24 separation system, UARX Space reinforces its integrated approach to spacecraft development, spanning the vehicle itself and the technology required for its deployment into orbit.
paras.zh: 该任务代表了西班牙空间技术能力的重大进步，展示了开发和集成空间运输和轨道运行关键技术的能力。通过将其 OTV 与其自己的 SAU&RON 24 分离系统相结合，UARX Space 强化了其航天器开发的集成方法，涵盖航天器本身及其部署到轨道所需的技术。

paras.en: OSSIE-D also highlights the importance of collaboration between specialized companies across the European space industry. For this mission, DHV Technology designed, qualified and manufactured the vehicle’s complete electrical power subsystem, including the solar arrays, Power Conditioning and Distribution Unit (PCDU), main battery modules, SADA (Solar Array Drive Assembly) and additional supporting subsystems required to meet the mission’s power requirements.
paras.zh: OSSIE-D 还强调了欧洲航天工业专业公司之间合作的重要性。对于此次任务，DHV Technology 设计、鉴定和制造了车辆的完整电力子系统，包括太阳能电池阵列、功率调节和配电单元 (PCDU)、主电池模块、SADA（太阳能阵列驱动组件）以及满足任务电力要求所需的其他支持子系统。

paras.en: “OSSIE-D represents a milestone for the Spanish aerospace industry and shows how collaboration between companies with complementary capabilities can turn ambitious missions into reality. DHV Technology has been a key partner, with its expertise, highly reliable solutions and team commitment making a significant contribution to the mission’s energy capabilities. This partnership also highlights the potential of the Spanish space sector to innovate and compete at both European and global level,” said Dr. Andrés Villa, CTO and Co-Founder of UARX Space.
paras.zh: UARX Space 首席技术官兼联合创始人 Andrés Villa 博士表示：“OSSIE-D 代表了西班牙航空航天业的一个里程碑，展示了具有互补能力的公司之间的合作如何能够将雄心勃勃的任务变为现实。DHV Technology 一直是关键合作伙伴，其专业知识、高度可靠的解决方案和团队承诺为任务的能源能力做出了重大贡献。这种合作伙伴关系还凸显了西班牙航天部门在欧洲和全球层面的创新和竞争潜力。”

paras.en: Following launch, DHV Technology’s electrical power subsystem is operating nominally in orbit, starting from the generation of the power with the solar arrays, control and distribution with the PCDU and storage with the battery, including initial telemetry which confirms that the system is performing as expected. This represents an important milestone for DHV Technology’s engineering team and for the OSSIE-D mission as a whole.
paras.zh: 发射后，DHV Technology 的电力子系统名义上在轨道上运行，从太阳能电池阵列发电、PCDU 控制和分配以及电池存储开始，包括确认系统按预期运行的初始遥测。这对于 DHV Technology 的工程团队和整个 OSSIE-D 任务来说是一个重要的里程碑。

paras.en: “Seeing the full electrical power subsystem fully developed by DHV for OSSIE-D operating as expected in orbit is an important milestone for our team and for our collaboration with UARX Space,” said Dr. Vicente Díaz, Managing Director and Co-Founder of DHV Technology. “This achievement reflects the close cooperation between both engineering teams and the work invested throughout the design, manufacturing, testing and integration phases. We are proud to contribute to this mission and look forward to OSSIE-D continuing to deliver positive results for UARX Space and all the partners involved.”
paras.zh: DHV Technology 董事总经理兼联合创始人 Vicente Díaz 博士表示：“看到 DHV 完全开发的用于 OSSIE-D 的完整电力子系统在轨道上按预期运行，对于我们的团队以及我们与 UARX Space 的合作来说是一个重要的里程碑。” “这一成就反映了两个工程团队之间的密切合作以及在整个设计、制造、测试和集成阶段所投入的工作。我们很自豪能为这一任务做出贡献，并期待 OSSIE-D 继续为 UARX Space 和所有相关合作伙伴带来积极的成果。”

paras.en: Beyond supplying the electrical power subsystem, DHV Technology is using OSSIE-D as a platform to test innovative technological concepts in orbit. The results obtained during the mission will help increase the technological maturity of several of the company’s solutions, extending the value of the mission beyond its immediate operational objectives. These developments include novel electrical interconnection methods, improved solar panel deployment and hinge mechanisms, as well as advanced photovoltaic technologies.
paras.zh: 除了提供电力子系统之外，DHV Technology 还使用 OSSIE-D 作为在轨测试创新技术概念的平台。任务期间获得的结果将有助于提高公司多个解决方案的技术成熟度，使任务的价值超出其直接运营目标。这些发展包括新颖的电气互连方法、改进的太阳能电池板部署和铰链机构以及先进的光伏技术。

paras.en: The collaboration between UARX Space and DHV Technology underscores the importance of combining specialized engineering capabilities to deliver increasingly advanced space missions. While UARX Space leads the development of the OTV and its deployment architecture, DHV Technology’s electrical power subsystem provides a critical element for the vehicle’s operation while enabling the evaluation of new technologies under real space operating conditions.
paras.zh: UARX Space 和 DHV Technology 之间的合作强调了结合专业工程能力来交付日益先进的太空任务的重要性。虽然 UARX Space 引领 OTV 及其部署架构的开发，但 DHV Technology 的电力子系统为车辆的运行提供了关键要素，同时能够在真实的空间运行条件下评估新技术。

paras.en: OSSIE-D therefore represents progress on two fronts: it strengthens UARX Space’s capabilities and position in the in-space transportation sector, while providing an opportunity to validate technologies that could support future missions. The combination of an OTV developed in Spain, a proprietary separation system and a complete electrical power subsystem supplied by DHV Technology demonstrates the potential of Spain’s space industry to deliver increasingly complex technological projects.
paras.zh: 因此，OSSIE-D 代表了两个方面的进展：它增强了 UARX Space 在太空运输领域的能力和地位，同时提供了验证可支持未来任务的技术的机会。西班牙开发的 OTV、专有的分离系统和 DHV Technology 提供的完整电力子系统的结合展示了西班牙航天工业交付日益复杂的技术项目的潜力。

articles.title: Cosmo Bee to flight-test Honeybee Hall thruster with D-Orbit in 2027
articles.author: Cosmo Bee

paras.en: Daejeon, Republic of Korea – October 14, 2026: South Korean space electric propulsion startup Cosmo Bee plans to conduct an in-orbit flight test of its 10 mN-class Honeybee Hall thruster system in October 2027 through a service agreement with D-Orbit.
paras.zh: 韩国大田 – 2026 年 10 月 14 日：韩国太空电力推进初创公司 Cosmo Bee 计划通过与 D-Orbit 签订的服务协议，于 2027 年 10 月对其 10 mN 级 Honeybee Hall 推进器系统进行在轨飞行测试。

paras.en: Honeybee is a 10 mN-class Hall thruster system under development by Cosmo Bee for small satellites operating in LEO constellations.
paras.zh: Honeybee 是 Cosmo Bee 正在为在 LEO 星座运行的小型卫星开发的 10 mN 级霍尔推进器系统。

paras.en: “In-orbit validation is an essential step as we prepare to bring Honeybee to the commercial market,” said Dongha Park, co-founder and CEO of Cosmo Bee. “D-Orbit is an ideal partner to help us achieve that goal.”
paras.zh: Cosmo Bee 联合创始人兼首席执行官 Dongha Park 表示：“在轨验证是我们准备将 Honeybee 推向商业市场的重要一步。” “D-Orbit 是帮助我们实现这一目标的理想合作伙伴。”

paras.en: “Hosting in-orbit demonstrations is one of the core services we offer aboard ION,” said Matteo Lorenzoni, Director of the Orbital Access Business Unit at D-Orbit. “Honeybee will operate in the real space environment, with our mission operations team supporting the test throughout, so Cosmo Bee comes away with the performance data it needs to take the thruster to market.” This test will evaluate Honeybee’s key performance parameters, including thrust and specific impulse, under various operating conditions.
paras.zh: “举办在轨演示是我们在 ION 上提供的核心服务之一，”D-Orbit 轨道接入业务部总监 Matteo Lorenzoni 说道。 “Honeybee 将在真实的太空环境中运行，我们的任务运营团队全程支持测试，因此 Cosmo Bee 可以获得将推进器推向市场所需的性能数据。”该测试将评估 Honeybee 在各种操作条件下的关键性能参数，包括推力和比冲量。

paras.en: “For satellite operators choosing a propulsion system, flight heritage is often what decides the purchase”, commented Matteo Zeni, Head of Sales of D-Orbit’s Orbital Access Business Unit. “Our in-orbit demonstration service gives technology developers like Cosmo Bee a direct route to space and the data they need to move from qualification to a commercial product. We look forward to flying Honeybee next year.”
paras.zh: “对于选择推进系统的卫星运营商来说，飞行传统往往是决定购买的因素”，D-Orbit 轨道接入业务部销售主管 Matteo Zeni 评论道。 “我们的在轨演示服务为 Cosmo Bee 等技术开发人员提供了直接进入太空的途径，以及他们从资格认证转向商业产品所需的数据。我们期待明年让 Honeybee 飞行。”

paras.en: Through the partnership, Cosmo Bee plans to establish flight heritage for Honeybee while preparing for the system’s commercial introduction in 2027. The company intends to make Honeybee available to satellite operators and mission developers seeking electric propulsion systems for small spacecraft.
paras.zh: 通过此次合作，Cosmo Bee 计划为 Honeybee 建立飞行遗产，同时为 2027 年该系统的商业推出做准备。该公司打算将 Honeybee 提供给卫星运营商和寻求小型航天器电力推进系统的任务开发商。

paras.en: Cosmo Bee was founded in July 2023 as a spin-off from the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST), building on electric propulsion research conducted by Professor Wonho Choe’s team since 2003.
paras.zh: Cosmo Bee 成立于 2023 年 7 月，是韩国科学技术院 (KAIST) 的一个衍生公司，其基础是 Wonho Choe 教授团队自 2003 年以来进行的电力推进研究。

paras.en: In November 2025, the company launched its first space mission, K-HERO, a 3U CubeSat designed to demonstrate the operation of a 150 W-class Hall thruster in orbit. The spacecraft was launched aboard South Korea’s KSLV-2 launch vehicle.
paras.zh: 2025 年 11 月，该公司发射了其首次太空任务 K-HERO，这是一颗 3U 立方体卫星，旨在演示 150 W 级霍尔推进器在轨道上的运行。该航天器是由韩国的 KSLV-2 运载火箭发射升空的。

paras.en: In June 2026, the Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA) designated Cosmo Bee’s 10 mN-class Hall thruster and hollow cathode technologies as “New Space Technologies.” The company also raised $5 million in a Series A funding round that month.
paras.zh: 2026 年 6 月，韩国宇宙航空管理局 (KASA) 将 Cosmo Bee 的 10 mN 级霍尔推进器和空心阴极技术指定为“新空间技术”。该公司还在当月的 A 轮融资中筹集了 500 万美元。

paras.en: “Cosmo Bee is growing alongside the rapidly expanding demand for LEO satellite constellations in South Korea,” Park said. “We hope Honeybee can support customers developing the next generation of small satellite constellations.”
paras.zh: Park 表示：“随着韩国对 LEO 卫星星座需求的快速增长，Cosmo Bee 也在不断发展。” “我们希望 Honeybee 能够支持客户开发下一代小型卫星星座。”

articles.title: Flexell Space and ALATYR Sign MoU to Explore Solar Power Solutions for Orbital Data Centers
articles.author: Flexell Space

paras.en: – Collaboration to assess next-generation ultralight solar cells for space-based computing infrastructure
paras.zh: – 合作评估用于天基计算基础设施的下一代超轻太阳能电池

paras.en: – Partnership brings together Korean space energy technology and French orbital infrastructure expertise
paras.zh: – 合作伙伴关系汇集了韩国空间能源技术和法国轨道基础设施专业知识

paras.en: Bremen, Germany – Flexell Space, a space energy company, announced that it has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with ALATYR, a French company developing orbital data centers, to explore solar power solutions for space-based computing infrastructure.
paras.zh: 德国不来梅 – 空间能源公司 Flexell Space 宣布与开发轨道数据中心的法国公司 ALATYR 签署了一份谅解备忘录 (MoU)，共同探索用于天基计算基础设施的太阳能解决方案。

paras.en: The collaboration will assess the potential application of Flexell Space’s next-generation solar cell technology to orbital infrastructure designed for large-scale computing and data storage. The companies intend to exchange technical requirements relating to power demand and operating conditions and explore opportunities for future joint development and validation.
paras.zh: 此次合作将评估 Flexell Space 的下一代太阳能电池技术在专为大规模计算和数据存储而设计的轨道基础设施中的潜在应用。两家公司打算交换有关电力需求和运行条件的技术要求，并探索未来联合开发和验证的机会。

paras.en: ALATYR develops orbital data centers designed to support artificial intelligence (AI) computing and mission-critical workloads. Its CITADEL modular infrastructure architecture and BYLD robotic system are designed to enable assembly, maintenance, and upgrades in orbit. The architecture separates the service life of the supporting infrastructure from the replacement cycle of computing hardware, enabling computing modules to be renewed in orbit while retaining the infrastructure that powers, cools, and supports them.
paras.zh: ALATYR 开发轨道数据中心，旨在支持人工智能 (AI) 计算和关键任务工作负载。其 CITADEL 模块化基础设施架构和 BYLD 机器人系统旨在实现在轨组装、维护和升级。该架构将支持基础设施的使用寿命与计算硬件的更换周期分开，使计算模块能够在轨道上更新，同时保留为其供电、冷却和支持的基础设施。

paras.en: Reliable power generation is essential to making orbital data centers viable. As these facilities grow, solar power systems must address not only electrical performance but also mass, launch and deployment efficiency, manufacturing costs, and long-term reliability.
paras.zh: 可靠的发电对于轨道数据中心的可行性至关重要。随着这些设施的发展，太阳能系统不仅必须解决电气性能问题，还必须解决质量、发射和部署效率、制造成本和长期可靠性问题。

paras.en: Flexell Space is developing next-generation space solar cells based on CIGS (copper indium gallium selenide) and perovskite technologies. With a focus on lightweight, flexible designs and large-area manufacturing, the company aims to provide power solutions for satellites and larger space infrastructure. Through the collaboration, Flexell Space intends to gain a clearer understanding of orbital data center requirements and assess how its technology could support this emerging application.
paras.zh: Flexell Space 正在开发基于 CIGS（铜铟镓硒）和钙钛矿技术的下一代太空太阳能电池。该公司专注于轻量化、灵活设计和大面积制造，旨在为卫星和更大的空间基础设施提供电源解决方案。通过此次合作，Flexell Space 打算更清楚地了解轨道数据中心的要求，并评估其技术如何支持这一新兴应用。

paras.en: “This MoU marks an important milestone in strengthening cooperation between Korea and Europe, particularly France, in space energy and infrastructure,” said Kyumin Lee, Business Development Manager at Flexell Space. “By combining our next-generation solar cell technology with ALATYR’s orbital infrastructure expertise, we aim to build a lasting partnership and lay the groundwork for joint development and validation of power solutions for future orbital data centers.”
paras.zh: Flexell Space 业务开发经理 Kyumin Lee 表示：“这份谅解备忘录标志着韩国与欧洲（特别是法国）在空间能源和基础设施领域加强合作的一个重要里程碑。” “通过将我们的下一代太阳能电池技术与 ALATYR 的轨道基础设施专业知识相结合，我们的目标是建立持久的合作伙伴关系，并为未来轨道数据中心电力解决方案的联合开发和验证奠定基础。”

paras.en: He added, “By bringing together our complementary capabilities, we aim to establish a practical foundation for future development and validation.”
paras.zh: 他补充道：“通过整合我们的互补能力，我们的目标是为未来的开发和验证奠定实用的基础。”

paras.en: “Our orbital infrastructure is designed to serve successive generations of computing hardware,” said Emeric Lhomme, Chief Executive Officer of ALATYR. “That makes solar cell efficiency and longevity central to our approach: our power systems must continue to deliver reliable performance as computing modules are replaced and upgraded. With Flexell Space, we will explore how next-generation lightweight solar technologies could meet the demands of that extended service life.”
paras.zh: ALATYR 首席执行官埃默里克·洛姆 (Emeric Lhomme) 表示：“我们的轨道基础设施旨在为连续几代的计算硬件提供服务。” “这使得太阳能电池的效率和寿命成为我们方法的核心：随着计算模块的更换和升级，我们的电力系统必须继续提供可靠的性能。通过 Flexell Space，我们将探索下一代轻型太阳能技术如何满足延长使用寿命的需求。”

paras.en: The companies plan to begin by exchanging information on their technologies and development priorities, followed by a phased assessment of solar cell and power system compatibility. Specific development activities and validation approaches will be discussed through subsequent technical consultations.
paras.zh: 两家公司计划首先交换有关技术和开发优先事项的信息，然后对太阳能电池和电力系统的兼容性进行分阶段评估。具体的开发活动和验证方法将通过后续技术磋商进行讨论。

paras.en: Flexell Space is a space energy company that originated as an internal venture at Hanwha Systems. The company develops next-generation space solar cells and power solutions based on CIGS and perovskite technologies, with a focus on low-cost, large-area, ultralight products. Through collaboration with global partners, Flexell Space is advancing the commercialization of solar cell technologies for satellites and a broad range of space infrastructure.
paras.zh: Flexell Space 是一家空间能源公司，最初是韩华系统公司的内部合资企业。该公司开发基于CIGS和钙钛矿技术的下一代空间太阳能电池和电源解决方案，重点是低成本、大面积、超轻产品。通过与全球合作伙伴的合作，Flexell Space 正在推进卫星太阳能电池技术和广泛的空间基础设施的商业化。

paras.en: ALATYR is a French company developing a new layer of critical digital infrastructure in space. The company designs orbital data centers that evolve with computing technology, rather than being replaced with each hardware generation. Its infrastructure is designed to remain productive over the long term and expand with demand, creating a lasting extension of the cloud in orbit to increase computing capacity and strengthen the resilience of essential digital services worldwide.
paras.zh: ALATYR 是一家法国公司，正在开发太空关键数字基础设施的新层。该公司设计的轨道数据中心随着计算技术的发展而发展，而不是随着每一代硬件的发展而更换。其基础设施旨在长期保持生产力并根据需求进行扩展，在轨道上创建云的持久扩展，以提高计算能力并增强全球基本数字服务的弹性。

articles.title: Thank You for Doing NASA Science!

paras.en: It’s Thanksgiving time, and we’re giving thanks to you for doing NASA Science with us! You and NASA’s other volunteers have enabled an incredible banquet of discoveries—by taking data, analyzing data, writing code, writing papers, and even inventing your own science projects. Whether you’re an expert participant or someone who’s just started your science journey, we’re deeply grateful for your help.
paras.zh: 感恩节到了，我们感谢您与我们一起进行 NASA 科学活动！您和 NASA 的其他志愿者通过获取数据、分析数据、编写代码、撰写论文，甚至发明自己的科学项目，实现了一场令人难以置信的发现盛宴。无论您是专家参与者还是刚刚开始科学之旅的人，我们都非常感谢您的帮助。

paras.en: Here are a few more messages of gratitude our scientists sent in to share with you.
paras.zh: 以下是我们的科学家发送来与您分享的更多感谢信息。

paras.en: Chihoko Cullens, principal investigator (PI) of the Space Cloud Watch project, said: “Thank you to Pirjo Koski, Huub Eggen, and Brian Scott! Pirjo posts beautiful Noctilucent Cloud photos and has introduced us to other cloud databases in the Netherlands. Huub goes beyond basic data requested by us and actively discusses his observations providing helpful insights. Brian contributes consistently and has provided us with useful time-lapse videos. All three volunteers have consistently provided much needed data and have contributed their time in developing our Field Guide that now helps new citizen scientists correctly identify and report their observations. We are grateful for their contributions.”
paras.zh: 太空云观察项目首席研究员 (PI) Chihoko Cullens 表示：“感谢 Pirjo Koski、Huub Eggen 和 Brian Scott！Pirjo 发布了漂亮的夜光云照片，并向我们介绍了荷兰的其他云数据库。Huub 超出了我们要求的基本数据，并积极讨论他的观察结果，提供了有用的见解。Brian 始终如一地做出贡献，为我们提供了有用的延时视频。所有三名志愿者都始终如一地提供了急需的数据，并为开发我们的领域贡献了自己的时间。现在可以帮助新公民科学家正确识别和报告他们的观察结果，我们感谢他们的贡献。”

paras.en: Ryan Scott from the Open Science Data Repository Analysis Working Groups (OSDR AWGs) project said: “A cohort of high school students took NASA’s free Machine Learning for Space Biology course and then kept working as citizen science volunteers. Guided by OSDR AWG members who also gave their time freely, they mined open-access retinal data from the International Space Station (ISS) Rodent Research-9 Mission in the NASA Open Science Data Repository and trained a machine learning ensemble that separates oxidative damage from cell death in the eyes of space-flown mice, now published in the scientific journal npj Microgravity: Machine learning ensemble reveals distinct molecular pathways of retinal damage in spaceflown mice. Every citizen science student co-author earned authorship, and many of those listed above started college this fall with a NASA publication already behind them. Thanks to Aditi Adapala, Mushtaq Ali, Naomi Z. Chang, Sophie Cai, Margaret Hitt, Anishka Jain, Matthew Lin, MarcAnthony Paolieri Della Monica, Elior Paley, Rudransh Pathak, Shawnak Samaddar, Shriya Sawant, Zhihan Shi, Rohin Sood, Fabian P. Uribe, Maxwell Volkan, and Jessica Wu, plus OSDR AWG members Anna Lewkowicz, Sunny Narayanan, Daniya Thomas, Ethan Waisberg, Pinar Avci, Joshua Ong, Marshall Tabetah, Richard Barker, Lauren Sanders, and Xiao Wen ‘Vivien’ Mao.”
paras.zh: 开放科学数据存储库分析工作组 (OSDR AWGs) 项目的 Ryan Scott 表示：“一群高中生参加了 NASA 的免费空间生物学机器学习课程，然后继续担任公民科学志愿者。在 OSDR AWG 成员的指导下，他们也免费投入了时间，在 NASA 开放科学数据存储库中挖掘了来自国际空间站 (ISS) 啮齿动物研究 9 任务的开放获取视网膜数据，并训练了一个机器学习集合，可以将氧化损伤与细胞死亡区分开来。太空飞行小鼠眼中的情况，现已发表在科学杂志 npj Microgravity：机器学习整体揭示了太空飞行小鼠视网膜损伤的独特分子途径。每位公民科学学生的合著者都获得了署名权，上面列出的许多人今年秋天开始上大学，并已在 NASA 的出版物上发表文章，这要感谢 Aditi Adapala、Mushtaq Ali、Naomi Z. Chang、Sophie Cai、Margaret Hitt、Anishka Jain、Matthew Lin 和 MarcAnthony。 Paolieri Della Monica、Elior Paley、Rudransh Pathak、Shawnak Samaddar、Shriya Sawant、Zhihan Shi、Rohin Sood、Fabian P. Uribe、Maxwell Volkan 和 Jessica Wu，以及 OSDR AWG 成员 Anna Lewkowicz、Sunny Narayanan、Daniya Thomas、Ethan Waisberg、Pinar Avci、Joshua Ong、Marshall Tabetah、Richard Barker、Lauren Sanders、和小文‘Vivien’Mao。”

paras.en: Kyra Shaw, project coordinator for Snapshot Wisconsin at the Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources, said: “Our team has a Thanksgiving thank-you message for Snapshot volunteer Tim Sparks. Tim has been a dedicated Snapshot Wisconsin volunteer for nearly 10 years. Tim went above and beyond these past two years by helping to pilot test protocols and then joining the full launch for a new initiative, the Snapshot Phenology Project. Joining a select group of volunteers, Tim set up and is maintaining extra equipment to measure snow depth, temperature, and sound recordings at his Snapshot trail camera site. Thank you, Tim, for joining in our events, sending in your favorite photos, and going the extra mile to make the Snapshot Phenology Project a success!”
paras.zh: 威斯康星州自然资源部 Snapshot Wisconsin 项目协调员凯拉·肖 (Kyra Shaw) 表示：“我们的团队向 Snapshot 志愿者蒂姆·斯帕克斯 (Tim Sparks) 发送了感恩节感谢信。近 10 年来，蒂姆一直是威斯康星州 Snapshot 的热心志愿者。在过去的两年里，蒂姆超越了过去两年，帮助试点测试协议，然后参与了一项新计划“快照物候学项目”的全面启动。蒂姆与一组精选的志愿者一起，建立了他正在维护额外的设备来测量雪深、温度和声音记录，蒂姆，感谢您参加我们的活动，发送您最喜欢的照片，并为使快照物候学项目取得成功而付出更多努力！”

paras.en: Benjamin Fernando from the Impact Flash! project said: "Thank you to everyone who’s been sending in images of the Moon! A special thanks to Joerg Tomczak, who helped us with the Artemis II campaign!”
paras.zh: 《冲击闪电》中的本杰明·费尔南多！该项目表示：“感谢所有发送月球图像的人！特别感谢 Joerg Tomczak，他帮助我们完成了 Artemis II 活动！”

paras.en: Rachael Mady from the Chesapeake Water Watch project said: “We are so thankful for all of our volunteers! Since 2021, volunteers have been with us every step of the way and have made Chesapeake Water Watch possible. The Chesapeake Bay is the nation's largest estuary, and we had people all over submitting observations and helping us cross our 6,000 observation milestone this year. While the project may be wrapping up, the impact that our volunteers have on improving the health of the Bay will continue for years to come. Thanks for all that you do!”
paras.zh: 切萨皮克水观察项目的 Rachael Mady 表示：“我们非常感谢所有志愿者！自 2021 年以来，志愿者一直陪伴在我们的每一步，使切萨皮克水观察成为可能。切萨皮克湾是美国最大的河口，我们各地的人们提交了观测结果，帮助我们今年跨越了 6,000 次观测的里程碑。虽然该项目可能即将结束，但我们的志愿者对改善感谢你们所做的一切，海湾的健康将持续多年！”

paras.en: Marc Kuchner, from the Backyard Worlds: Planet 9 science team, said: “Thank you to Prateek Singh for creating new tools for astronomy and for helping us lead our Space Apps challenge! Thank you to Bruce Baller and Katharina Doll for sharing their lists of brown dwarf discoveries and for inspiring all of us! Thank you to Frank Kiwy for his latest batch of python tools – shared with everyone – that dig through Pan-STARRS, WISE, SIMBAD, Gaia DR3, CatWISE, and NSC DR2 data! Thank you to Michiharu Hyogo for keeping the new publications coming, Hugo Durantini Luca, Jim Rabe, and Lisa Stiller for helping keep us all connected, Peter Jalowiczor for traveling around the world in the snow, and to Farid Cedeno and Martin Bilsing for teaching others about our project!”
paras.zh: 来自 Backyard Worlds: Planet 9 科学团队的 Marc Kuchner 表示：“感谢 Prateek Singh 为天文学创建了新工具，并帮助我们领导了 Space Apps 挑战！感谢 Bruce Baller 和 Katharina Doll 分享了他们的褐矮星发现清单，并激励了我们所有人！感谢 Frank Kiwy 与大家分享的最新一批 Python 工具，这些工具通过 Pan-STARRS、WISE、SIMBAD、Gaia 进行了挖掘DR3、CatWISE 和 NSC DR2 数据！感谢 Michiharu Hyogo 不断推出新出版物，感谢 Hugo Durantini Luca、Jim Rabe 和 Lisa Stiller 帮助我们保持联系，感谢 Peter Jalowiczor 在雪地里环游世界，感谢 Farid Ceden 和 Martin Bilsing 向其他人传授我们的项目！”

paras.en: Emma Yates, PI of the Ozone Where We Live (OWWL) project, said: “We have developed an amazing collaboration with Quest Science Center, a non-profit that among many other things supports high school students interested in the Earth’s climate. One of the aspects of Quest is to develop student-run studies by pairing high school students with mentors. OWWL has been working with these students and their Quest mentors to study air quality in the Tri-Valley Region in California (Bay Area into San Joaquin Valley). We designed a mini field campaign over the month of August, with 12 science flights and ground-based sensors at participants' homes. I know the students (and mentors) would get a kick out of seeing their work highlighted by NASA!”
paras.zh: 我们居住的臭氧 (OWWL) 项目的主要负责人艾玛·耶茨 (Emma Yates) 表示：“我们与 Quest 科学中心建立了令人惊叹的合作关系，这是一个非盈利组织，除其他外，还为对地球气候感兴趣的高中生提供支持。Quest 的一个方面是通过将高中生与导师配对来开展学生开展的研究。OWWL 一直在与这些学生及其 Quest 导师合作，研究加利福尼亚州三谷地区（从湾区到圣路易斯）的空气质量。 Joaquin Valley）。我们在 8 月份设计了一场小型实地活动，在参与者家中进行了 12 次科学飞行，我知道学生（和导师）会因为看到 NASA 强调的他们的工作而感到高兴！”

paras.en: Everyone can join the fun and make a lasting mark on NASA science. You’ll find all our open opportunities at https://science.nasa.gov/citizen-science/. Happy Thanksgiving!
paras.zh: 每个人都可以加入其中，并在 NASA 科学事业上留下持久的印记。您可以在 https://science.nasa.gov/citizen-science/ 上找到我们所有的开放机会。感恩节快乐！

articles.title: NASA Sets Coverage for Northrop Grumman CRS-25 Launch, Prelaunch
articles.author: Jessica Taveau

paras.en: NASA, Northrop Grumman, and SpaceX are targeting no earlier than 10:47 a.m. EST, Sunday, Nov. 29, for the next launch delivering science investigations, supplies, and equipment to the International Space Station. The agency also will hold a prelaunch media teleconference on Monday, Nov. 23.
paras.zh: NASA、诺斯罗普·格鲁曼公司和 SpaceX 的目标是在美国东部时间 11 月 29 日星期日上午 10:47 之前进行下一次发射，向国际空间站运送科学调查、物资和设备。该机构还将于 11 月 23 日星期一举行启动前媒体电话会议。

paras.en: Filled with approximately 11,000 pounds of cargo, the Northrop Grumman Cygnus XL spacecraft, aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, will launch from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. The mission is known as NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25, or Northrop Grumman CRS-25.
paras.zh: 装载着约 11,000 磅货物的诺斯罗普·格鲁门天鹅座 XL 航天器搭载 SpaceX 猎鹰 9 号火箭，将从佛罗里达州卡纳维拉尔角太空部队站的 40 号航天发射场发射升空。该任务被称为 NASA 诺斯罗普·格鲁曼商业补给服务 25，或诺斯罗普·格鲁曼 CRS-25。

paras.en: After arriving at the International Space Station, NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, who are living and working aboard the space station, will use the Canadarm2 robotic arm to capture the Cygnus XL on Tuesday, Dec. 1. Ground controllers then will install it to the Unity module’s Earth-facing port for cargo unloading.
paras.zh: 抵达国际空间站后，在空间站生活和工作的 NASA 宇航员杰西卡·沃特金斯 (Jessica Watkins) 和卢克·德莱尼 (Luke Delaney) 将于 12 月 1 日星期二使用 Canadaarm2 机械臂捕获 Cygnus XL。然后地面控制器将其安装到 Unity 模块面向地球的端口，用于货物卸载。

paras.en: NASA’s live launch and docking coverage will stream through a variety of platforms. Learn where to watch online:
paras.zh: NASA 的现场发射和对接报道将通过各种平台进行直播。了解在哪里在线观看：

paras.en: Highlights of space station research and technology demonstrations being delivered aboard this Cygnus XL spacecraft include experiments to improve drug delivery for cancer and osteoarthritis, predict cancer spread, and advance treatments for muscle loss, as well as improve radiation sensing and advance food production for future long-duration missions.
paras.zh: Cygnus XL 航天器上进行的空间站研究和技术演示的亮点包括改善癌症和骨关节炎药物输送、预测癌症扩散、推进肌肉损失治疗、以及改善辐射传感和促进未来长期任务的粮食生产等实验。

paras.en: The spacecraft is scheduled to remain at the orbiting laboratory until May 2027, then depart with several thousand pounds of disposal items and other unneeded cargo, burning up harmlessly during re-entry.
paras.zh: 该航天器计划将在轨道实验室停留到 2027 年 5 月，然后带着数千磅的处置物品和其他不需要的货物离开，并在重返大气层时无害地燃烧。

paras.en: Northrop Grumman named the spacecraft the S.S. James “Jim” A. Lovell in honor of the former NASA astronaut. Lovell flew four missions, including Gemini VII, Gemini XII, Apollo 8, and the Apollo 13 mission around the Moon.
paras.zh: 诺斯罗普·格鲁曼公司将这艘飞船命名为 S.S. James“Jim” A. Lovell，以纪念这位前 NASA 宇航员。洛弗尔执行了四次任务，包括双子座 7 号、双子座 12 号、阿波罗 8 号和阿波罗 13 号绕月任务。

paras.en: 12 p.m.: Prelaunch teleconference will stream on NASA’s YouTube channel with the following participants:
paras.zh: 中午 12 点：发射前电话会议将在 NASA 的 YouTube 频道上直播，与会者如下：

paras.en: - Gaurang Patel, operations integration manager, NASA’s Low Earth Orbit Program
paras.zh: - Gaurang Patel，美国宇航局近地轨道计划运营整合经理

paras.en: - Jennifer Buchli, chief scientist, NASA’s Low Earth Orbit Program
paras.zh: - Jennifer Buchli，美国宇航局近地轨道计划首席科学家

paras.en: - Dave Schiller, vice president, civil space and sciences, Northrop Grumman
paras.zh: - 戴夫·席勒 (Dave Schiller)，诺斯罗普·格鲁曼公司民用空间与科学副总裁

paras.en: - Jared Metter, director, flight reliability, SpaceX
paras.zh: - Jared Metter，SpaceX 飞行可靠性总监

paras.en: To participate in the teleconference, media must contact the NASA Johnson Space Center newsroom for call details by 11 a.m., Nov. 23, at: jsccommu@mail.nasa.gov or 281-483-5111. To ask questions, media must dial in no later than 10 minutes before the start of the call. The agency’s media credentialing policy is available online.
paras.zh: 要参加电话会议，媒体必须在 11 月 23 日上午 11 点之前联系 NASA 约翰逊航天中心新闻编辑室，了解通话详细信息，联系方式：jsccommu@mail.nasa.gov 或 281-483-5111。如需提问，媒体必须在通话开始前 10 分钟内拨通。该机构的媒体认证政策可在线获取。

paras.en: Additional prelaunch updates will be available on NASA’s space station blog.
paras.zh: 其他发射前更新将在 NASA 的空间站博客上提供。

paras.en: Launch day coverage of the mission will be available on the NASA website. Coverage will include live streaming and blog updates beginning no earlier than 10 a.m. on Nov. 29, as the countdown milestones occur. On-demand streaming video on NASA+ and photos of the launch will be available shortly after liftoff. For questions about countdown coverage, contact the NASA Kennedy Space Center newsroom at 321-867-2468. Follow countdown coverage on our International Space Station blog for updates.
paras.zh: 该任务的发射日报道将在美国宇航局网站上发布。报道将包括直播和博客更新，时间不早于 11 月 29 日上午 10 点，即倒计时里程碑的发生。 NASA+ 上的点播流媒体视频和发射照片将在升空后不久提供。有关倒计时报道的问题，请联系 NASA 肯尼迪航天中心新闻编辑室：321-867-2468。关注我们的国际空间站博客上的倒计时报道以获取更新。

paras.en: Members of the public can register to attend this launch virtually. NASA’s virtual guest program for this mission also includes curated launch resources, notifications about related opportunities or changes, and a stamp for the NASA virtual guest passport following launch.
paras.zh: 公众可以通过虚拟方式注册参加此次发布会。 NASA 针对此次任务的虚拟访客计划还包括精心策划的发射资源、有关相关机会或变化的通知，以及发射后为 NASA 虚拟访客护照盖上的印章。

paras.en: Let people know you’re watching the mission on X, Facebook, and Instagram by following and tagging these accounts:
paras.zh: 通过关注并标记这些帐户，让人们知道您正在 X、Facebook 和 Instagram 上观看此次任务：

paras.en: X: @NASA, @NASAKennedy, @NASASpaceOps, @Space_Station, @ISS National Lab
paras.zh: X：@NASA、@NASAKennedy、@NASASpaceOps、@Space_Station、@ISS 国家实验室

paras.en: Facebook: NASA, NASAKennedy, ISS, ISS National Lab
paras.zh: Facebook：NASA、NASAKennedy、ISS、ISS 国家实验室

paras.en: Instagram: @NASA, @NASAKennedy, @ISS, @ISSNationalLab
paras.zh: Instagram：@NASA、@NASAKennedy、@ISS、@ISSNationalLab

paras.en: Learn more about this commercial resupply services mission at:
paras.zh: 了解有关此商业补给服务任务的更多信息：

paras.en: joshua.a.finch@nasa.gov / james.j.russell@nasa.gov
paras.zh: joshua.a.finch@nasa.gov / james.j.russell@nasa.gov

articles.title: El Niño Rains Paint the Atacama

paras.en: Parts of the Atacama Desert in northern Chile, normally one of the driest places on Earth, turned red-purple, green, and white in austral spring 2026 following an unusually wet winter. The rain woke seeds lying dormant in the soil, setting off what scientists say may be the most extensive desierto florido, or “flowering desert,” of the satellite era.
paras.zh: 智利北部阿塔卡马沙漠的部分地区通常是地球上最干燥的地方之一，但在经历了异常潮湿的冬季后，2026 年南方春天变成了红紫色、绿色和白色。雨水唤醒了土壤中休眠的种子，科学家们称，这可能是卫星时代最广阔的沙漠，即“开花沙漠”。

paras.en: The rains came as El Niño was strengthening in the tropical Pacific. During an El Niño, the subtropical Pacific high that normally keeps the region dry weakens, while a blocking high tends to form in the South Pacific near the tip of South America. Together, these shifts push the Southern Hemisphere storm track equatorward.
paras.zh: 降雨到来之际，热带太平洋的厄尔尼诺现象正在加强。在厄尔尼诺现象期间，通常使该地区保持干燥的副热带太平洋高压减弱，而南太平洋靠近南美洲尖端的地方往往会形成阻塞高压。这些变化共同推动南半球风暴路径向赤道移动。

paras.en: Beginning in mid-July, a series of storm fronts fed by an atmospheric river brought one of the heaviest July rain events in decades to a long stretch of Chile, from the Atacama region south to Los Lagos, according to Chile’s national weather service (Dirección Meteorológica de Chile). In August, back-to-back winter storms blanketed parts of the Atacama Desert in rare snow.
paras.zh: 据智利国家气象局 (Dirección Meteorológica de Chile) 称，从 7 月中旬开始，由大气河推动的一系列风暴锋给智利从阿塔卡马地区以南到洛斯拉各斯的大部分地区带来了几十年来最严重的 7 月降雨事件之一。八月，接二连三的冬季风暴以罕见的降雪覆盖了阿塔卡马沙漠的部分地区。

paras.en: The spring blooms that followed are visible in these satellite image pairs, which show the desert at different stages of flowering on September 14 (left) and on October 24 (right). The OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 8 acquired the September images, and the OLI on Landsat 9 acquired the October images.
paras.zh: 在这些卫星图像对中可以看到随后的春季花朵，它们显示了沙漠在 9 月 14 日（左）和 10 月 24 日（右）不同开花阶段的情况。 Landsat 8 上的 OLI（操作陆地成像仪）获取了 9 月份的图像，Landsat 9 上的 OLI 获取了 10 月份的图像。

paras.en: The pair above shows a part of the desert about 30 kilometers (20 miles) southwest of Copiapó, near the eastern sector of Desierto Florido National Park. The red-purple areas prominent in the October 24 scene are vast blooms of pata de guanaco, most likely Cistanthe longiscapa or another Cistanthe species, according to Roberto Chávez, a remote sensing scientist at Pontificia Universidad Católica de Valparaíso.
paras.zh: 上图显示了科皮亚波西南约 30 公里（20 英里）处的部分沙漠，靠近佛罗里达沙漠国家公园东部。瓦尔帕莱索天主教大学遥感科学家罗伯托·查韦斯 (Roberto Chávez) 表示，10 月 24 日场景中突出的红紫色区域是大片的 pata de guanaco 花朵，很可能是长肉苁蓉或另一种肉苁蓉物种。

paras.en: Chávez and colleagues photographed the Cistanthe blooms (above) in the area that same day. They were in the field to study the bloom with satellite data, drones, and digital cameras. The project aims to use these data to map how the bloom’s biodiversity changes across space and over time, to inform land-use planners and conservation managers.
paras.zh: 查韦斯和同事当天在该地区拍摄了肉苁蓉花（上图）。他们在现场利用卫星数据、无人机和数码相机研究水华。该项目旨在利用这些数据绘制水华生物多样性如何随空间和时间变化的图谱，为土地利用规划者和保护管理者提供信息。

paras.en: The pair below shows another part of the blooming desert, about 50 kilometers (30 miles) southwest of Copiapó. It lies within a priority area of the desert cited for its biological significance, including the flowering landscape.
paras.zh: 下图显示的是盛开的沙漠的另一部分，位于科皮亚波西南约 50 公里（30 英里）处。它位于沙漠的优先区域内，因其具有生物学意义，包括开花景观。

paras.en: Cistanthe is abundant here in the October view, but the September scene (left) reveals another desert beauty. The green areas capped with white are blooms of suspiros, or Nolana, probably Nolana baccata, according to Andres Moreira-Muñoz, a scientist at Pontificia Universidad Católica de Valparaíso who studies plant geography. The researchers photographed the Nolana-covered hillsides below on September 24, 2026.
paras.zh: 十月的景色中肉苁蓉很丰富，但九月的景色（左）则展现出另一种沙漠之美。瓦尔帕莱索天主教大学研究植物地理学的科学家安德烈斯·莫雷拉-穆尼奥斯表示，白色覆盖的绿色区域是苏斯皮罗斯（Suspiros）或诺拉纳（Nolana）的花朵，可能是诺拉纳巴卡塔（Nolana baccata）。研究人员于 2026 年 9 月 24 日拍摄了下面诺拉纳覆盖的山坡。

paras.en: Satellite data have been key to understanding the Atacama’s blooms. A 2014 study used Landsat observations to map where flowering and fog-fed plants grow around the Copiapó dune field. And a 2019 study used NASA’s long-term vegetation record to identify 13 Atacama Desert blooms between 1981 and 2015.
paras.zh: 卫星数据是了解阿塔卡马花盛开的关键。 2014 年的一项研究利用陆地卫星观测结果绘制了科皮亚波沙丘周围开花植物和雾养植物生长位置的地图。 2019 年的一项研究利用 NASA 的长期植被记录识别出 1981 年至 2015 年间阿塔卡马沙漠的 13 次水华。

paras.en: Compared with those past blooms, the 2026 event stands out. “This instance of the ‘blooming desert’ phenomenon appears to be the most significant to date—in terms of its extent, intensity, and duration,” Moreira-Muñoz said, “at least since we began using remote sensing.”
paras.zh: 与以往的盛况相比，2026 年的盛会显得格外引人注目。莫雷拉-穆尼奥斯说：“就其范围、强度和持续时间而言，‘盛开的沙漠’现象似乎是迄今为止最重要的一次，至少自我们开始使用遥感以来是如此。”

paras.en: NASA Earth Observatory images by Michala Garrison, using Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey. Photos by Matías Pérez-Evens and Roberto O. Chávez/LabGRS-Instituto de Geografía- Pontificia Universidad Católica de Valparaíso, Chile, acquired during Fondecyt Regular Project 1251184 (ANID, Chile): Spatiotemporal variation of Flowering Desert biodiversity via multispectral remote sensing. Story by Kathryn Hansen.
paras.zh: NASA 地球观测站图像，由 Michala Garrison 使用美国地质调查局的陆地卫星数据拍摄。照片由 Matías Pérez-Evens 和 Roberto O. Chávez/LabGRS-Instituto de Geografía- Pontificia Universidad Católica de Valparaíso（智利）拍摄，在 Fondecyt 常规项目 1251184（ANID，智利）期间获得：通过多光谱遥感技术分析沙漠生物多样性的时空变化。凯瑟琳·汉森的故事。

paras.en: - Atlas Obscura (2024, May 10) Witness the Stunning and Ephemeral Desierto Florido. Accessed November 18, 2026.
paras.zh: - Atlas Obscura（2024 年，5 月 10 日）见证令人惊叹且短暂的佛罗里达州沙漠。访问日期：2026 年 11 月 18 日。

paras.en: - Biblioteca del Congreso Nacional de Chile/BCN (2023, June 12) Decree 12: Creates the “Flowering Desert National Park,” in the Commune and Province of Copiapó, Atacama Region. Accessed November 18, 2026.
paras.zh: - 智利国家会议图书馆/BCN（2023 年，6 月 12 日）第 12 号法令：在阿塔卡马地区科皮亚波公社和省创建“开花沙漠国家公园”。访问日期：2026 年 11 月 18 日。

paras.en: - Castro Avaria, C., et al. (2014) Detección del área con desierto florido en el territorio del Mar de Dunas de Atacama, mediante percepción remota. Revista de geografía Norte Grande, (57), 103-121.
paras.zh: - 卡斯特罗·阿瓦里亚 (Castro Avaria)，C. 等人。 (2014) 检测佛罗里达州阿塔卡马沙丘沿海地区的沙漠地区，并进行远程感知。 Revista de geografía Norte Grande，(57)，103-121。

paras.en: - Chávez, R.O., et al. (2019) GIMMS NDVI time series reveal the extent, duration, and intensity of “blooming desert” events in the hyper-arid Atacama Desert, Northern Chile. International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation, (76), 193-203.
paras.zh: - Chávez, R.O. 等人(2019) GIMMS NDVI 时间序列揭示了智利北部超干旱阿塔卡马沙漠“沙漠开花”事件的范围、持续时间和强度。国际应用地球观测和地理信息杂志，(76)，193-203。
