paras.zh: DealBook 峰会的亮点包括：

articles.title: Why so many critical tech outages are happening all at once

paras.en: Conspiracy theorists are having a field day. In the space of a week, Microsoft’s cloud software was unavailable for almost 24 hours, a malfunctioning telecommunications network brought U.S. air traffic to a standstill, a problem at JPMorgan Chase disrupted its services, and United Airlines struggled to get planes off the ground. Apple’s online services have ground to a halt, and the U.S. National Security Agency is dealing with an outage affecting its classified communications network.
paras.zh: 阴谋论者正在大肆狂欢。一周之内，微软的云软件几乎24小时无法使用，电信网络故障导致美国空中交通陷入瘫痪，摩根大通的问题扰乱了其服务，联合航空公司艰难地让飞机起飞。苹果的在线服务已经停止，美国国家安全局正在处理影响其机密通信网络的故障。

paras.en: So many major outages in such a short space of time inevitably raises questions. Is there something connecting these disparate incidents? Or are we simply noticing when things go wrong more often?
paras.zh: 在如此短的时间内发生如此多的重大停电不可避免地会引发问题。这些不同的事件之间有什么联系吗？或者我们只是注意到事情出问题的频率更高？

paras.en: In the immediate aftermath of some of these outages, fingers pointed at potential cyberattacks or artificial intelligence systems running amok. The available evidence supports neither: Microsoft says its problems weren’t caused by malicious activity or AI agents, and the Federal Aviation Administration has found no indication of a cyberattack. Apple’s outage followed an internal update, while the NSA said its problems arose during scheduled maintenance.
paras.zh: 在其中一些中断发生后，人们立即指责潜在的网络攻击或人工智能系统失控。现有证据并不支持这两者：微软表示，其问题不是由恶意活动或人工智能代理引起的，而且美国联邦航空管理局也没有发现网络攻击的迹象。苹果公司在内部更新后发生了故障，而美国国家安全局表示，问题是在定期维护期间出现的。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: There’s a paucity of proof that tech is becoming less reliable overall. Analysis by the Uptime Institute, a digital infrastructure tracker, found data center outage rates per site had fallen in 2026 for a fifth consecutive year.
paras.zh: 缺乏证据表明技术总体上变得越来越不可靠。数字基础设施跟踪机构 Uptime Institute 的分析发现，到 2026 年，每个站点的数据中心中断率已连续第五年下降。

paras.en: It’s tempting to read into the scale of the recent incidents and their frequency—but be wary, cautions Laura Nolan, a software reliability engineer at Trace Cognitive Engineering. If there are 52 major outages in a year, she explains, that doesn’t mean there’ll be one every week. There might be several in a matter of days, followed by weeks without any. “It doesn’t necessarily mean that it’s a shared causal factor,” she says.
paras.zh: Trace Cognitive Engineering 的软件可靠性工程师劳拉·诺兰 (Laura Nolan) 警告说，人们很容易了解最近事件的规模及其频率，但要小心。她解释说，如果一年内发生 52 次重大停电，并不意味着每周都会发生一次。几天之内可能会有几个，然后几周就没有了。 “这并不一定意味着这是一个共同的因果因素，”她说。

paras.en: Part of the problem is the complexity of the systems we’ve constructed—updating them invites errors. “When making changes in such systems, the results are often unpredictable,” says Nancy Leveson, a professor of aeronautics and astronautics at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, who studies system safety. Engineers have historically approached failures as a sequence of cause and effect, she explains, but our increasingly interconnected world also creates so-called emergent properties—outcomes that nobody intended and that can’t be understood by examining individual components alone.
paras.zh: 部分问题在于我们构建的系统的复杂性——更新它们会导致错误。 “在对此类系统进行更改时，结果往往是不可预测的，”研究系统安全的麻省理工学院航空航天教授南希·莱维森 (Nancy Leveson) 说。她解释说，工程师历来将故障视为一系列因果关系，但我们日益互联的世界也创造了所谓的突现属性，即没有人想要的结果，也无法通过单独检查单个组件来理解这些结果。

paras.en: Microsoft’s preliminary investigation, for example, shows an example of emergent properties writ large: a software bug introduced in July lay unnoticed until an ordinary change shifted more traffic to affected servers. Recovering from the issue took the best part of a day because restarting servers kept triggering the same fault.
paras.zh: 例如，微软的初步调查显示了一个明显的紧急属性的例子：7 月份引入的一个软件错误一直未被注意到，直到一个普通的更改将更多流量转移到受影响的服务器。从问题中恢复花了一天的时间，因为重新启动服务器不断触发相同的故障。

paras.en: The FAA’s November 13 failure was somewhat different. According to the agency, data flooded its telecommunications network during work that included installing a new router at a remote site in Arkansas. The disruption affected 17 of its 22 regional air traffic control centers, prompting a nationwide ground stop.
paras.zh: FAA 11 月 13 日的失败有所不同。据该机构称，在阿肯色州远程站点安装新路由器等工作期间，数据淹没了其电信网络。这次中断影响了 22 个地区空中交通管制中心中的 17 个，导致全国范围内停飞。

paras.en: Couldn’t this have been avoided? Nolan explains that it’s practically impossible to test changes on an exact replica of a live system. Testing environments are generally scaled down because of cost, meaning they can’t re-create every interaction between different pieces of infrastructure. “Nobody wants to pay twice for the same system,” she says.
paras.zh: 这难道就不能避免吗？诺兰解释说，在实时系统的精确副本上测试更改实际上是不可能的。由于成本原因，测试环境通常会缩小规模，这意味着它们无法重新创建不同基础设施之间的每次交互。 “没有人愿意为同一个系统支付两次费用，”她说。

paras.en: Kelly Shortridge, chief product officer at the infrastructure company Fastly and author of Security Chaos Engineering, suggests another possible reason for the uncanny timing: the annual rush to make software changes before companies freeze updates over the holiday period.
paras.zh: 基础设施公司 Fastly 的首席产品官兼《Security Chaos Engineering》一书的作者 Kelly Shortridge 提出了造成这种奇怪时机的另一个可能原因：每年公司都会在假期期间冻结更新之前急于进行软件更改。

paras.en: “In the weeks before the freeze, teams scramble to release everything at once,” she says, sometimes updating software that has gone without maintenance for years. Shortridge stresses this is a hypothesis rather than a smoking gun. But the failures seem to share “a routine change colliding with a certainty that had gone unchallenged long enough to gather dust,” she explains.
paras.zh: “在冻结之前的几周，团队争先恐后地立即发布所有内容，”她说，有时会更新多年来没有维护的软件。肖特里奇强调，这是一个假设，而不是铁证。但她解释说，这些失败似乎都有一个共同点：“例行公事的改变与长期未受挑战、已尘埃落定的确定性相冲突”。

paras.en: The issue is compounded by the fact that companies and governments have become accustomed to prioritizing speed and cost over preparing for failures. “As capabilities scale, losses and harm also scale,” says David Woods, professor emeritus of integrated systems engineering at the Ohio State University.
paras.zh: 由于公司和政府已经习惯于优先考虑速度和成本而不是为失败做好准备，这一事实使问题变得更加复杂。 “随着能力的扩大，损失和危害也会扩大，”俄亥俄州立大学集成系统工程名誉教授大卫·伍兹说。

paras.en: So how can we mitigate the dangers? Shortridge recommends isolating components so that one failure doesn’t bring everything else down and deliberately testing backup systems under stressful conditions. Leveson says engineering approaches need to look at the entire system holistically rather than treating every breakdown as an isolated technical fault. But bosses, Woods argues, don’t want to spend the time and money to fix something until it goes wrong. By the time the planes stop flying, it’s too late.
paras.zh: 那么我们怎样才能减轻危险呢？ Shortridge 建议隔离组件，以便一次故障不会导致其他所有组件瘫痪，并在压力条件下故意测试备份系统。莱维森表示，工程方法需要从整体上看待整个系统，而不是将每次故障视为孤立的技术故障。但伍兹认为，老板们不想花时间和金钱来修复问题，直到问题出现为止。当飞机停止飞行时，为时已晚。

paras.en: “Software incidents are actually inevitable,” Nolan says. The challenge is making sure the next one doesn’t bring everything else crashing down with it.
paras.zh: “软件事件实际上是不可避免的，”诺兰说。挑战在于确保下一个不会让其他一切都崩溃。

articles.title: Bernie Sanders previews Democratic investigations into RFK, Jr., amid nationwide measles outbreaks

paras.en: When Democrats take control of the Senate in the January, Secretary of Health and Human Services Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., will be a prime target for a key committee.
paras.zh: 当民主党在一月份控制参议院时，卫生与公众服务部部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪将成为一个关键委员会的首要目标。

paras.en: At a press briefing on Wednesday, Senator Bernie Sanders of Vermont, who is the current ranking member of the Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor and Pensions, hinted that Kennedy’s stewardship of the Department of Health and Human Services amid measles outbreaks that have been so severe that the U.S. lost its elimination status this week would warrant close examination.
paras.zh: 在周三的新闻发布会上，现任参议院健康、教育、劳工和养老金委员会高级成员、佛蒙特州参议员伯尼·桑德斯暗示，肯尼迪在麻疹疫情爆发期间对卫生与公众服务部的管理工作值得密切关注，麻疹疫情严重，美国本周失去了消除地位。

paras.en: “The idea that we have a secretary of health and human services who is into conspiracy theories has led us in a direction where, for the first time in God knows how long, we have lost our status as a measles-free country,” Sanders said. “That is certainly one area that needs investigation. There are many more.”
paras.zh: 桑德斯说：“我们的卫生与公众服务部部长热衷于阴谋论，这种想法已经把我们引向了一个方向，天知道我们有多久，第一次失去了无麻疹国家的地位。” “这当然是需要调查的一个领域。还有更多。”

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Sanders, an Independent who caucuses with the Democrats, extended an olive branch to the “Make America Healthy Again” (MAHA) movement.
paras.zh: 与民主党同组的独立人士桑德斯向“让美国再次健康”（MAHA）运动伸出了橄榄枝。

paras.en: “To the degree that we can work with MAHA people, we want to see good labeling on food packages that we don't have right now,” he said. “I would like to see junk food advertising off of the TV airwaves. So I think there are some areas that we can work with [them].”
paras.zh: “就我们可以与 MAHA 人员合作而言，我们希望在食品包装上看到我们目前还没有的良好标签，”他说。 “我希望在电视广播中看到垃圾食品广告。所以我认为我们可以在某些领域与[他们]合作。”

paras.en: Sanders refused to elaborate on any specific investigations into the Trump administration that may be coming in 2027, but he added that the Senate committee will scrutinize federal ties to the pharmaceutical and health insurance industries.
paras.zh: 桑德斯拒绝详细说明 2027 年可能对特朗普政府进行的任何具体调查，但他补充说，参议院委员会将审查联邦与制药和健康保险行业的关系。

paras.en: “You have this absurdity where people are filing claims for health care benefits that they had paid for, and they’re getting rejected. Meanwhile the insurance companies make huge profits,” Sanders said. “We’re also going to want to know why, when the federal government puts huge amounts of money into research and development for prescription drugs, taxpayers pay for that, [but] we end up paying the highest prices in the world for prescription drugs.”
paras.zh: “这是荒谬的，人们提出索赔他们已经支付的医疗保健福利，但他们被拒绝了。与此同时，保险公司赚取了巨额利润，”桑德斯说。 “我们还想知道为什么当联邦政府投入大量资金用于处方药的研发时，纳税人为此买单，但我们最终却为处方药支付了世界上最高的价格。”

paras.en: The committee will also focus on legislation pertaining to one of Sanders’s longtime pet issues, universal health care, he said. Regardless of who is named Senate majority leader, Sanders said, he believes a “Medicare for All” bill will come up for a Senate vote within a year of Democrats retaking Congress.
paras.zh: 他说，该委员会还将重点关注与桑德斯长期关注的问题之一——全民医疗保健有关的立法。桑德斯表示，无论谁被任命为参议院多数党领袖，他相信“全民医疗保险”法案将在民主党重新夺回国会后一年内提交参议院投票。

paras.en: Support for a single-payer Medicare for All option has grown among the general population and the Democratic caucus over the past few years, but any legislation passed in Congress could be vetoed by President Donald Trump.
paras.zh: 过去几年，普通民众和民主党核心小组对单一付款人全民医疗保险选项的支持有所增加，但国会通过的任何立法都可能被唐纳德·特朗普总统否决。

paras.en: Editor’s Note (11/18/26): This is a developing story and may be updated.
paras.zh: 编者注（11/18/26）：这是一个正在发展的故事，可能会更新。

articles.title: The Vulcan rocket failure could haunt U.S. spaceflight for years to come

paras.en: On the afternoon of November 15, the United Launch Alliance’s (ULA’s) Vulcan rocket suffered a mission-ending malfunction 10 minutes after blasting off, destroying its payload of satellites for broadband Internet from Amazon’s Amazon Leo. This marks the first total mission failure for ULA, a joint Boeing–Lockheed Martin venture seen as a space industry stalwart—and is also a significant setback for Amazon.
paras.zh: 11 月 15 日下午，联合发射联盟 (ULA) 的火神火箭在发射 10 分钟后发生故障，导致任务结束，亚马逊的 Amazon Leo 宽带互联网卫星的有效载荷被摧毁。这标志着 ULA 的首次任务彻底失败，ULA 是波音与洛克希德·马丁公司的合资企业，被视为航天工业的中坚力量，这对亚马逊来说也是一个重大挫折。

paras.en: Both companies are struggling to catch up to their launch and satellite communications competitor, SpaceX. The failure also may affect NASA’s race against China to land astronauts on the moon and build a base there. And it has national security implications as well because the U.S. Space Force is, alongside Amazon, Vulcan’s main customer.
paras.zh: 两家公司都在努力追赶其发射和卫星通信竞争对手 SpaceX。这次失败还可能影响美国宇航局与中国在将宇航员送上月球并在那里建立基地的竞赛。它还具有国家安全影响，因为美国太空军和亚马逊一样，都是 Vulcan 的主要客户。

paras.en: The loss is only the latest in a longer string of interconnected misfortunes. This was intended to be Vulcan’s triumphant return to flight: the launcher had been grounded after its previous flight, in February, had worrisome malfunctions in a Northrop Grumman–made solid rocket booster. On its first stage, Vulcan also uses two advanced methane-burning BE-4 engines, which are supplied by Blue Origin, another would-be SpaceX rival bankrolled by Amazon’s Jeff Bezos. And Blue Origin is recovering from its own catastrophe in May, when its massive New Glenn rocket—also equipped with BE-4 engines—blew up during a launchpad test. New Glenn is still grounded, but company officials are targeting January 2027 for its return to flight.
paras.zh: 这次损失只是一连串相互关联的不幸中的最新一起。这原本是火神号成功重返飞行的机会：在二月份的上一次飞行中，诺斯罗普·格鲁曼公司制造的固体火箭助推器出现了令人担忧的故障，发射器因此被停飞。在第一阶段，Vulcan 还使用了两台先进的燃烧甲烷的 BE-4 发动机，这些发动机由 Blue Origin 提供，Blue Origin 是 SpaceX 的另一个潜在竞争对手，由亚马逊的 Jeff Bezos 资助。蓝色起源公司正在从 5 月份的灾难中恢复过来，当时其巨大的新格伦火箭（也配备了 BE-4 发动机）在发射台测试中爆炸。新格伦号仍处于停飞状态，但公司官员预计 2027 年 1 月恢复飞行。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: For its part, SpaceX so far seems on track to continue its dominance, with a historic first successful catch of its Starship on its Texas launch tower after that fully reusable vehicle flawlessly delivered a batch of the company’s Starlink satellites into orbit during the test flight. Stymied by Vulcan’s mounting mishaps, Amazon’s competing Amazon Leo service is far behind schedule in its rollout, and the company had already booked 37 more Vulcan launches to deliver more of its satellites into orbit.
paras.zh: 就 SpaceX 而言，到目前为止，它似乎有望继续保持其主导地位，在完全可重复使用的运载器在试飞期间将一批该公司的 Starlink 卫星完美地送入轨道后，其 Starship 在德克萨斯州的发射塔上历史性地首次成功捕获。由于 Vulcan 事故不断增多，亚马逊的竞争对手 Amazon Leo 服务的推出远远落后于计划，该公司已经预订了 37 次 Vulcan 发射，以将更多卫星送入轨道。

paras.en: If Blue Origin’s BE-4 engines are the culprits for Vulcan’s failure, this could compound delays for the company’s Blue Moon lunar lander, which NASA needs for its Artemis program moon landings and must launch on New Glenn rockets. And Vulcan’s second stage, called the Centaur V, is also integral to future flights of the space agency’s Artemis-supporting Space Launch System (SLS) rocket; any significant problems with ULA’s Centaur V could lead to more delays for future SLS launches.
paras.zh: 如果 Blue Origin 的 BE-4 发动机是 Vulcan 失败的罪魁祸首，这可能会加剧该公司 Blue Moon 月球着陆器的延误，NASA 需要该着陆器用于其 Artemis 计划登月，并且必须使用 New Glenn 火箭发射。 Vulcan 的第二级称为 Centaur V，也是该航天局支持阿耳忒弥斯的太空发射系统 (SLS) 火箭未来飞行的组成部分。 ULA Centaur V 的任何重大问题都可能导致未来 SLS 发射的更多延误。

paras.en: Julie Arnold, a ULA spokesperson, tells Scientific American that “ULA exists to provide assured access to space for our nation and for the customers who depend on us. That purpose is why we take on some of the hardest missions in spaceflight and why we hold ourselves to the standard of mission success. Today we did not meet that standard.” The comments reiterated what the company previously posted on X.
paras.zh: ULA 发言人朱莉·阿诺德 (Julie Arnold) 告诉《科学美国人》，“ULA 的存在是为了为我们的国家和依赖我们的客户提供进入太空的保障。这个目的就是为什么我们承担一些最艰巨的太空飞行任务，也是为什么我们坚持任务成功的标准。今天我们没有达到这个标准。”这些评论重申了该公司之前在 X 上发布的内容。

paras.en: Vulcan’s return to flight on Sunday initially looked like a routine launch from Space Launch Complex 41 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. Unlike ULA’s four previous Vulcan launches, this one was the first to use six solid rocket boosters rather than two or four. Unlike some of those earlier launches, this one saw no obvious problems with those boosters, which peeled off and fell back to Earth as planned about one and a half minutes into the flight.
paras.zh: 周日，火神号重返飞行，最初看起来像是从佛罗里达州卡纳维拉尔角太空部队站 41 号航天发射场进行的例行发射。与 ULA 之前的四次火神发射不同，这次是第一次使用六个固体火箭助推器，而不是两个或四个。与之前的一些发射不同，这次的助推器没有出现明显的问题，助推器在飞行大约一分半钟后就按计划脱落并落回地球。

paras.en: But at about five minutes after takeoff, Vulcan’s BE-4-powered first stage fired 30 seconds longer than planned. “That’s a long time, because in launches, everything is timed to the second,” says Paul Ronney, an aerospace engineer at the University of Southern California. It suggests that the first stage underperformed and had to continue firing to compensate, he says.
paras.zh: 但在起飞后约 5 分钟，Vulcan 的 BE-4 动力第一级点火时间比计划晚了 30 秒。南加州大学航空航天工程师保罗·罗尼 (Paul Ronney) 表示：“这是一个很长的时间，因为在发射过程中，一切都精确到秒。”他说，这表明第一级表现不佳，必须继续点火来弥补。

paras.en: ULA appeared to confirm as much in a statement posted on its website on November 17: “Early indications are that just after liftoff the launch vehicle experienced low [first-stage] performance, resulting in stage separation occurring when the vehicle was low in altitude and below minimal velocity to reach orbit,” it said.
paras.zh: ULA 似乎在 11 月 17 日在其网站上发布的一份声明中证实了这一点：“早期迹象表明，运载火箭在升空后不久，[第一级]性能较低，导致运载火箭在高度较低且低于到达轨道的最低速度时发生级分离，”它说。

paras.en: “Blue Origin is working closely with ULA to investigate and determine the root cause,” a company spokesperson told Scientific American. NASA’s chief Jared Isaacman also expressed support for the investigation in a response on X to ULA’s public statement on the anomaly: “The team at NASA is available to assist in all matters related to the investigation and remediation effort,” Isaacman said. “Artemis, Moon Base, and the nation need ULA. We are in your corner and here to help.”
paras.zh: “蓝色起源正在与 ULA 密切合作，调查并确定根本原因，”公司发言人告诉《科学美国人》。 NASA 局长贾里德·艾萨克曼 (Jared Isaacman) 在 X 上对 ULA 关于该异常现象的公开声明的回应中也表达了对调查的支持：“NASA 的团队可以协助处理与调查和补救工作相关的所有事务，”艾萨克曼说。 “阿尔忒弥斯、月球基地和国家都需要 ULA。我们站在你这边，随时为你提供帮助。”

paras.en: SpaceX head Elon Musk also weighed in, replying to ULA’s post, “Hope you are back to flight soon.”
paras.zh: SpaceX 负责人埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 也发表了自己的看法，他在回复 ULA 的帖子时表示：“希望你很快就能重返飞行轨道。”

paras.en: Although ULA’s investigation is ongoing, an additional update from the company released on 11 A.M. EST on November 18 said that the first stage’s issues appeared to be “the result of inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines” rather than a problem with the engines themselves.
paras.zh: 尽管 ULA 的调查仍在进行中，但该公司已于上午 11 点发布了额外的更新信息。美国东部时间 11 月 18 日表示，第一阶段的问题似乎是“车辆向 BE-4 发动机供应燃油不足的结果”，而不是发动机本身的问题。

paras.en: ULA and Blue Origin have long been working to catch up with SpaceX’s overwhelming lead in launch services, as have other providers such as Rocket Lab, whose first launch of its new Neutron rocket is delayed until 2027. In the meantime, regardless of whether its customers are ready to lose it, SpaceX is planning to retire its prolific Falcon 9 rocket in favor of the company’s still experimental Starship. Yet even if Starship works as SpaceX plans, its launches may mostly be filled with SpaceX’s own cargo—Starlink satellites, as well the company’s proposed orbital data centers. NASA may use modified Starships for multiple Artemis moon missions, including Artemis IV, which is slated for 2028 and is planned to be the first crewed lunar landing since the Apollo era.
paras.zh: ULA 和 Blue Origin 长期以来一直在努力追赶 SpaceX 在发射服务方面的压倒性领先地位，Rocket Lab 等其他提供商也是如此，其新型中子火箭的首次发射被推迟到 2027 年。与此同时，无论其客户是否准备好失去它，SpaceX 都计划退役其多产的猎鹰 9 号火箭，转而使用该公司仍在实验中的星际飞船。然而，即使 Starship 按照 SpaceX 的计划进行，其发射的也可能主要是 SpaceX 自己的货物——星链卫星，以及该公司提议的轨道数据中心。 NASA 可能会使用改装后的星际飞船执行多项阿尔忒弥斯登月任务，其中包括定于 2028 年进行的阿尔忒弥斯 IV，计划成为阿波罗时代以来的首次载人登月。

paras.en: SpaceX’s Starship pivot poses challenges for potential government and commercial customers, says Clayton Swope, deputy director of the Aerospace Security Project at the Center for Strategic & International Studies, a Washington, D.C.–based think tank. “The first thing is: Does the ‘bus’ have an extra seat? And the second is: Can you fit your butt in that seat? I don’t think SpaceX is going to make you a bespoke bus seat,” he says. Starship presently employs a novel deployment bay that is custom-made to accommodate Starlink satellites—and that its customers’ payloads may not be able to use.
paras.zh: 华盛顿智库战略与国际研究中心航空航天安全项目副主任克莱顿·斯沃普 (Clayton Swope) 表示，SpaceX 的星舰转向给潜在的政府和商业客户带来了挑战。 “第一件事是：‘巴士’有额外的座位吗？第二件事是：你能把屁股放在那个座位上吗？我不认为 SpaceX 会给你定制巴士座位，”他说。 Starship 目前采用了一种新颖的部署舱，该部署舱是为容纳 Starlink 卫星而定制的，但其客户的有效载荷可能无法使用。

paras.en: That means that if SpaceX phases out the Falcon 9 before Vulcan, New Glenn, Neutron, or other rockets are ready to fill the gap, that could create a launch crisis. “In some ways, this is where we’ve been for 10 years, crossing our fingers and hoping there’s an increase in competition in launch,” Swope says.
paras.zh: 这意味着，如果 SpaceX 在 Vulcan、New Glenn、Neutron 或其他火箭准备好填补空缺之前逐步淘汰 Falcon 9，可能会引发发射危机。 “从某种程度上来说，这就是我们 10 年来一直在做的事情，祈祷发布过程中的竞争会更加激烈，”斯沃普说道。

articles.title: What the Trump administration’s focus on AI and quantum means for science
articles.author: Emily Conover

paras.en: Many fields of science have struggled under the second Trump administration, with funding cuts and delays plaguing research in fields such as public health and climate science. But some topics have found firmer footing, including artificial intelligence and quantum science.
paras.zh: 在特朗普第二届政府领导下，许多科学领域都陷入困境，公共卫生和气候科学等领域的研究受到资金削减和延误的困扰。但一些话题已经找到了更坚实的基础，包括人工智能和量子科学。

paras.en: These technologies, along with supercomputing, “are going to be the three legs of the stool that is going to transform how science and engineering is done,” says Darío Gil, undersecretary for science at the U.S. Department of Energy.
paras.zh: 美国能源部负责科学事务的副部长达里奥·吉尔 (Darío Gil) 表示，这些技术与超级计算“将成为改变科学和工程实施方式的三条腿”。

paras.en: In November 2025, President Donald Trump issued an executive order to launch the Genesis Mission, a $5 billion whole-of-government effort to advance science via artificial intelligence. The initiative began with the DOE but has since expanded to more than 15 federal agencies.
paras.zh: 2025 年 11 月，唐纳德·特朗普总统发布行政命令，启动“创世纪任务”，这是一项耗资 50 亿美元的政府整体计划，旨在通过人工智能推进科学发展。该倡议始于美国能源部，但后来扩展到超过 15 个联邦机构。

paras.en: In June, the president issued an executive order that aims to accelerate the development of tools such as quantum computers, quantum sensors and quantum networks. And in July, the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy issued a 123-page report describing its vision for a “golden age” of federal science, in which agencies align investments in research and development with administration priorities.
paras.zh: 6月，总统发布了一项行政命令，旨在加速量子计算机、量子传感器和量子网络等工具的开发。 7 月，白宫科学技术政策办公室发布了一份 123 页的报告，描述了其对联邦科学“黄金时代”的愿景，其中各机构将研发投资与政府优先事项结合起来。

paras.en: Federal agencies spent some $4.2 billion on AI R&D in 2025, according to an arm of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy that quantifies such investments.
paras.zh: 根据白宫科学技术政策办公室量化此类投资的部门的数据，联邦机构到 2025 年将在人工智能研发上花费约 42 亿美元。

paras.en: Many scientists are enthusiastic about the opportunities for AI and quantum research. But some caution that a measured approach is needed. “My strongest opinion … is that I want to see all fields of science supported,” says Brad Marston, a physicist at Brown University and president of the American Physical Society. “Priorities have to be chosen, but getting a good balance is important, because you never know where some advance will come from.”
paras.zh: 许多科学家对人工智能和量子研究的机会充满热情。但一些人警告说，需要采取谨慎的方法。 “我最强烈的观点……是我希望看到所有科学领域都得到支持，”布朗大学物理学家、美国物理学会主席布拉德·马斯顿说。 “必须选择优先事项，但取得良好的平衡很重要，因为你永远不知道一些进展将从何而来。”

paras.en: Through Genesis, the DOE plans to use its troves of data as well as experimental and computing facilities to produce a common set of AI tools and a shared ecosystem for science. “That’s conceptually a very powerful idea,” says astronomer Rachel Mandelbaum of Carnegie Mellon University in Pittsburgh. “And if it pans out as intended, it could drive great advances in science and technology.”
paras.zh: 通过 Genesis，美国能源部计划利用其大量数据以及实验和计算设施来生产一套通用的人工智能工具和一个共享的科学生态系统。 “从概念上讲，这是一个非常强大的想法，”匹兹堡卡内基梅隆大学的天文学家雷切尔·曼德尔鲍姆说。 “如果它如预期那样成功，它将推动科学技术的巨大进步。”

paras.en: This year, DOE funded nearly 300 projects through Genesis — including one led by Mandelbaum. Her team’s effort aims to unify immense datasets from astronomical facilities around the world, such as the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument and the Zwicky Transient Facility. That would enable AI models to be trained on the data, which could help uncover hidden astronomical insights.
paras.zh: 今年，能源部通过 Genesis 资助了近 300 个项目，其中包括曼德尔鲍姆领导的一个项目。她的团队致力于统一来自世界各地天文设施的海量数据集，例如维拉·C·鲁宾天文台、暗能量光谱仪和兹威基瞬态设施。这将使人工智能模型能够根据数据进行训练，这有助于揭示隐藏的天文见解。

paras.en: Other projects include efforts to accelerate nuclear reactor development, create simulations of the U.S. electric grid and study nuclear fusion. And federal agencies including the National Science Foundation and the National Institutes of Health have launched their own Genesis efforts, centered around the mission’s National Science and Technology Challenges, which include topics in health, biology, energy, space, national security and more.
paras.zh: 其他项目包括加速核反应堆开发、创建美国电网模拟以及研究核聚变。美国国家科学基金会和美国国立卫生研究院等联邦机构也启动了自己的创世纪计划，围绕该任务的国家科学和技术挑战，其中包括健康、生物学、能源、太空、国家安全等主题。

paras.en: Many scientists were already wielding AI in their work. But Genesis “really did create an inflection point,” says John Sarrao, director of SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory in Menlo Park, Calif. SLAC is now involved with 20 Genesis projects and leads two.
paras.zh: 许多科学家已经在他们的工作中运用人工智能。但位于加利福尼亚州门洛帕克的 SLAC 国家加速器实验室主任 John Sarrao 表示，Genesis“确实创造了一个拐点”。SLAC 目前参与了 20 个 Genesis 项目，并领导了其中两个项目。

paras.en: Compared with AI, quantum technologies are less mature. With quantum computing, “we’re still at mile one or two or three of a marathon,” says Celia Merzbacher, executive director of the Quantum Economic Development Consortium, a coalition of public and private institutions that works to bolster quantum tech in the United States. Nevertheless, researchers hope the two technologies can amplify one another. AI could help design and develop quantum computers, for example, while quantum computing shows promise for efficiently tackling certain machine learning problems.
paras.zh: 与人工智能相比，量子技术还不太成熟。量子经济发展联盟（Quantum Economic Development Consortium）执行董事西莉亚·梅尔兹巴赫（Celia Merzbacher）表示，对于量子计算，“我们仍处于马拉松比赛的一英里、二英里或三英里处”。该联盟是一个由公共和私人机构组成的联盟，致力于支持美国的量子技术。尽管如此，研究人员希望这两种技术能够相互增强。例如，人工智能可以帮助设计和开发量子计算机，而量子计算有望有效解决某些机器学习问题。

paras.en: Accordingly, several Genesis projects involve quantum error correction, quantum sensors and quantum materials. And the DOE’s Quantum Genesis initiative aims to develop scientifically useful, error-corrected quantum computers by 2028.
paras.zh: 因此，几个 Genesis 项目涉及量子纠错、量子传感器和量子材料。美国能源部的量子创世纪计划旨在到 2028 年开发出具有科学用途、可纠错的量子计算机。

paras.en: AI and quantum were not always hot topics. “Both of those areas … were kind of backwaters until recent advances,” Marston says. Before the development of deep neural networks, for example, AI was mostly a curiosity. “It points to the importance of having a balanced approach to science funding,” he says. What starts as an obscure scientific specialty may suddenly explode into wide relevance.
paras.zh: 人工智能和量子并不总是热门话题。马斯顿说：“在最近取得进展之前，这两个领域都处于停滞状态。”例如，在深度神经网络发展之前，人工智能主要是一种好奇心。 “这表明了科学资助采取平衡方法的重要性，”他说。一开始作为一个默默无闻的科学专业可能会突然爆发出广泛的相关性。

paras.en: In the context of limited resources, prioritizing one area of research necessitates deprioritizing another. While some funding for the DOE’s portion of Genesis came from the One Big Beautiful Bill passed in 2025, much of the rest came from the DOE’s budget.
paras.zh: 在资源有限的情况下，优先考虑一个研究领域就需要降低另一个研究领域的优先顺序。虽然能源部 Genesis 部分的部分资金来自 2025 年通过的《一项美丽的大法案》，但其余大部分来自能源部的预算。

paras.en: As excited as Mandelbaum is about Genesis, she is concerned about funding for non-AI related work. A cosmology grant her group received from the DOE didn’t align with Genesis mission priorities and was reduced this year, she says. “If the reality is that some of this [funding] is coming out of the baseline research budget in my field, then I think that it would be beneficial for the DOE to engage the scientific community about those trade-offs,” Mandelbaum says.
paras.zh: 尽管曼德尔鲍姆对《创世纪》感到兴奋，但她也担心非人工智能相关工作的资金问题。她说，她的团队从美国能源部获得的宇宙学资助与创世纪任务的优先事项不符，今年被减少了。 “如果现实情况是部分[资金]来自我所在领域的基线研究预算，那么我认为能源部让科学界参与这些权衡将是有益的，”曼德尔鲍姆说。

paras.en: In response to these concerns, Gil says that the money going to Genesis from the DOE’s Office of Science — about $400 million so far — is small compared to the office’s total FY2026 budget of $8.4 billion.
paras.zh: 针对这些担忧，吉尔表示，与该办公室 2026 财年 84 亿美元的总预算相比，能源部科学办公室向 Genesis 提供的资金（迄今为止约为 4 亿美元）很小。

paras.en: Sarrao says that it’s important to build on the momentum of Genesis while still supporting the DOE’s core research. His impression is that things are trending in the right direction. “Are there really exciting opportunities? Yes, 100 percent,” Sarrao says. “Are there risks if you get the balance wrong? Equally well, 100 percent.”
paras.zh: Sarrao 表示，在继续支持能源部核心研究的同时，在 Genesis 的发展势头基础上发展非常重要。他的印象是事情正在朝着正确的方向发展。 “真的有令人兴奋的机会吗？是的，100%，”萨拉奥说。 “如果你的平衡错了，会有风险吗？同样好，100%。”

articles.title: Cracks in public health grew in 2026
articles.author: Erin Garcia de Jesús

paras.en: Public health is invisible — until it’s not.
paras.zh: 公共卫生是看不见的——直到它变得不可见。

paras.en: It’s tough to tally the injuries or deaths that don’t happen thanks to seat belts, lead testing, smoking bans and vaccines. “It is the invisibility paradox,” says Georges Benjamin, CEO of the American Public Health Association in Washington, D.C. “We are invisible because when our best work is done, nothing happens.”
paras.zh: 很难统计由于安全带、铅检测、禁烟令和疫苗而没有发生的伤害或死亡。 “这是隐形悖论，”华盛顿特区美国公共卫生协会首席执行官乔治·本杰明说，“我们是隐形的，因为当我们完成最好的工作时，什么也没有发生。”

paras.en: But when disaster strikes — say, an outbreak or a pandemic — people take notice. This year’s outbreaks of measles, Ebola, hantavirus and cyclosporiasis brought recent federal reductions into focus — and exposed cracks in a system that aims to keep people healthy. For years, that system functioned “reasonably well” despite chronic underfunding, Benjamin says. “But since the Trump administration has come on board, they have really made the system at all levels much more dysfunctional.”
paras.zh: 但当灾难发生时——比如爆发或流行病——人们就会注意到。今年麻疹、埃博拉、汉坦病毒和环孢子虫病的爆发使联邦最近的削减成为焦点，并暴露了旨在保持人们健康的系统中的漏洞。本杰明说，多年来，尽管长期资金不足，该系统仍运行“相当良好”。 “但自从特朗普政府上任以来，他们确实让各个层面的系统功能更加失调。”

paras.en: In 2025, the second Trump administration instituted sweeping federal funding cuts and layoffs, dismantled the global health–focused U.S. Agency for International Development and withdrew the United States from the World Health Organization. Officials reversed some of those changes in the wake of lawsuits and public backlash. But the damage persists.
paras.zh: 2025年，特朗普第二届政府实施了全面的联邦资金削减和裁员，解散了专注于全球健康的美国国际开发署，并使美国退出世界卫生组织。在诉讼和公众强烈反对后，官员们撤销了其中一些变化。但损害仍然存在。

paras.en: Two stalwarts of U.S. public health — the Food and Drug Administration and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention — have lost between 20 and 30 percent of their staff, due largely to layoffs and early retirements. They have had to scale back, pause or cancel crucial disease-tracking programs at home and abroad. Some CDC divisions don’t have enough staff to function. And both agencies have cut funding to the local governments and nonprofits that shoulder much of the nation’s public health work.
paras.zh: 美国公共卫生的两个中坚力量——食品药品监督管理局和疾病控制与预防中心——已经失去了 20% 到 30% 的员工，主要原因是裁员和提前退休。他们不得不缩减、暂停或取消国内外重要的疾病追踪项目。疾控中心的一些部门没有足够的人员来运作。这两个机构都削减了对承担国家大部分公共卫生工作的地方政府和非营利组织的资助。

paras.en: Combined with deep cuts to international aid, that has stymied efforts to contain infectious disease outbreaks around the world, with Ebola in particular going undetected for months, public health experts say.
paras.zh: 公共卫生专家表示，加上国际援助的大幅削减，这阻碍了世界各地遏制传染病爆发的努力，尤其是埃博拉病毒几个月来都未被发现。

paras.en: Domestically, 2026 saw a record-breaking measles outbreak, with some 5,412 confirmed cases as of November 12. That’s more than double last year’s count, and it is the highest number of annual cases since 1991. In mid November, the Pan American Health Organization determined that measles is again endemic to the United States and has stripped the country of its elimination status.
paras.zh: 在国内，2026年麻疹疫情创纪录，截至11月12日约有5,412例确诊病例。这一数字是去年的两倍多，也是自1991年以来年度病例数最高的一次。11月中旬，泛美卫生组织确定麻疹再次在美国流行，并取消了该国的消除地位。

paras.en: Against a backdrop of shifting federal vaccine guidance, fewer children are receiving the MMR shot that prevents measles. Roughly 92 percent of kindergartners across the United States had gotten the vaccine in the 2025–2026 school year, down from 95 percent in the 2019–2020 school year, according to the CDC. At least 95 percent of people in a community need to be vaccinated to prevent the measles virus from sparking an outbreak.
paras.zh: 在联邦疫苗指导方针发生变化的背景下，接受预防麻疹的 MMR 疫苗的儿童越来越少。根据 CDC 的数据，2025-2026 学年，美国约 92% 的幼儿园学生接种了疫苗，低于 2019-2020 学年的 95%。社区中至少 95% 的人需要接种疫苗，以防止麻疹病毒引发疫情。

paras.en: “The fact that we are spending so much time and energy [on measles] when we have a reliable vaccine is very disconcerting,” says Lori Handy, a pediatric infectious diseases physician and associate director of the Vaccine Education Center at Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia.
paras.zh: “当我们拥有可靠的疫苗时，我们却在[麻疹]上花费了如此多的时间和精力，这一事实非常令人不安，”儿科传染病医生、费城儿童医院疫苗教育中心副主任洛里·汉迪(Lori Handy)说。

paras.en: The CDC has not responded to Science News requests for an interview.
paras.zh: 疾病预防控制中心尚未回应《科学新闻》的采访请求。

paras.en: Such issues do not bode well for the future. Public health is tested during times of crisis, and the world will eventually face another pandemic, says Michael Osterholm, director of the Center for Infectious Disease Research and Policy at the University of Minnesota in Minneapolis. “We’ve not responded [to the 2026 outbreaks] in a way that would give me confidence that the public health system … is prepared for what’s coming down the pike.”
paras.zh: 这些问题对未来来说并不是好兆头。明尼阿波利斯明尼苏达大学传染病研究与政策中心主任迈克尔·奥斯特霍尔姆表示，公共卫生在危机时期受到考验，世界最终将面临另一场大流行。 “我们（对 2026 年疫情的）反应方式还没有让我相信公共卫生系统……已经为即将发生的事情做好了准备。”

paras.en: On the heels of multiple 2025 outbreaks, measles continued to wallop parts of the United States this year. Communities in South Carolina, Utah and Wisconsin have been among the hardest hit, with sporadic outbreaks also popping up in other states. Until August, however, none of this year’s outbreaks had turned deadly. That all changed in Pennsylvania.
paras.zh: 继 2025 年多次爆发疫情之后，麻疹今年继续席卷美国部分地区。南卡罗来纳州、犹他州和威斯康星州的社区受到的打击最为严重，其他州也出现了零星疫情。然而，直到八月，今年的疫情爆发都没有导致致命。这一切在宾夕法尼亚州发生了变化。

paras.en: About a quarter of this year’s cases stem from an outbreak in central Pennsylvania, where the virus has spread widely in communities with low vaccination rates. Since April, seven people in the state have died, including two infants too young to be vaccinated. The CDC has so far attributed just six deaths to measles, despite the insistence of Pennsylvania state public health officials. Three children died of measles in November in New York and Wisconsin.
paras.zh: 今年约四分之一的病例源于宾夕法尼亚州中部的疫情爆发，该病毒在疫苗接种率较低的社区广泛传播。自四月以来，该州已有七人死亡，其中包括两名因年龄太小而无法接种疫苗的婴儿。尽管宾夕法尼亚州公共卫生官员坚持认为，迄今为止，疾病预防控制中心仅将六例死亡归因于麻疹。 11 月，纽约州和威斯康星州的三名儿童死于麻疹。

paras.en: As of November 12, U.S. health officials recorded 5,412 measles cases for 2026. The last time this many cases were recorded was 1991, nearly a decade before the disease was eliminated from the country.
paras.zh: 截至 11 月 12 日，美国卫生官员记录了 2026 年麻疹病例 5,412 例。上一次记录如此多病例是在 1991 年，距离该疾病从该国消灭已近十年。

paras.en: Measles spreads like wildfire, and one sick person can infect more than a dozen others in an unvaccinated community. While milder symptoms include fever and a hallmark full-body rash, infection can lead to pneumonia, brain swelling and even death. Statistically, the virus kills one to three out of every 1,000 infected people.
paras.zh: 麻疹像野火一样传播，在未接种疫苗的社区中，一名病人可能会感染十几个人。虽然较轻微的症状包括发烧和标志性的全身皮疹，但感染可能导致肺炎、脑肿胀甚至死亡。据统计，每 1000 名感染者中就有 1 到 3 人死于该病毒。

paras.en: The United States eliminated measles in 2000, thanks to the MMR vaccine. “Elimination” means the virus was not spreading widely, and any outbreaks were controlled within a year. But dropping vaccination rates have reestablished the conditions to sustain multiple outbreaks — and may have done so as early as 2022, researchers reported in August in Nature Medicine.
paras.zh: 得益于 MMR 疫苗，美国于 2000 年消灭了麻疹。 “消灭”是指病毒没有大范围传播，疫情在一年内得到控制。但研究人员 8 月在《自然·医学》杂志上报道称，疫苗接种率的下降已经重新创造了维持多次疫情爆发的条件，而且最早可能在 2022 年就实现了这一点。

paras.en: In the wake of losing measles elimination status in November, beating back the the virus again “will take a true change in the public’s trust of health care,” Handy says. That means figuring out how to get people vaccinated — and to encourage them to work with public health officials on testing and contact tracing after exposure.
paras.zh: 汉迪说，在十一月失去麻疹消除状态后，再次击退病毒“将真正改变公众对医疗保健的信任”。这意味着弄清楚如何让人们接种疫苗，并鼓励他们与公共卫生官员合作，在接触后进行检测和接触者追踪。

paras.en: Fading protection from measles, mumps and rubella
paras.zh: 麻疹、腮腺炎和风疹的褪色防护

paras.en: During the 2009–2010 school year, 20 states had MMR vaccination rates equal to or above 95 percent among kindergartners. Just 10 states hit that threshold for 2025–2026, and 18 states had vaccination rates below 90 percent.
paras.zh: 2009-2010 学年，20 个州的幼儿园儿童 MMR 疫苗接种率等于或高于 95%。 2025-2026 年，只有 10 个州达到了这一阈值，其中 18 个州的疫苗接种率低于 90%。

paras.en: It has been more than three decades since measles caused widespread outbreaks in the United States, and many have never experienced the devastation it can cause. When one community hears about an outbreak halfway across the country, “it still feels very foreign,” Handy says. When the threat feels far away, people are not likely to line up to get a vaccine. Yet measles is so contagious that one unvaccinated traveler can bring the virus back home and spark an outbreak in their own community.
paras.zh: 麻疹在美国大面积爆发已有三十多年了，许多人从未经历过它可能造成的破坏。汉迪说，当一个社区听说全国各地爆发疫情时，“仍然感觉很陌生”。当威胁感觉很遥远时，人们不太可能排队接种疫苗。然而，麻疹的传染性如此之大，以至于一名未接种疫苗的旅行者可以将病毒带回家，并在自己的社区引发疫情爆发。

paras.en: Even with the recent spike in cases, there is hope vaccination rates can catch up, says Cornell University epidemiologist Ana Bento. She points to California and New York, which experienced outbreaks in 2015 and 2018; they ended non-medical exemptions for school vaccinations shortly thereafter. Both states now have vaccination rates above 95 percent in kindergartners. “This is not a tipping point where there’s no coming back,” Bento says.
paras.zh: 康奈尔大学流行病学家安娜·本托表示，即使最近病例激增，疫苗接种率也有望赶上。她指出，加利福尼亚州和纽约州曾在 2015 年和 2018 年爆发过疫情；此后不久，他们就终止了学校疫苗接种的非医疗豁免。目前这两个州的幼儿园疫苗接种率均超过 95%。 “这并不是一个无法挽回的转折点，”本托说。

paras.en: If measles exposed the consequences of long-simmering vaccine hesitancy, then this summer’s cyclosporiasis outbreak was a quick lesson in food safety screening.
paras.zh: 如果说麻疹暴露了长期对疫苗犹豫不决的后果，那么今年夏天的环孢子虫病爆发就是食品安全筛查的一个快速教训。

paras.en: In June, Michigan detected its first cases of the foodborne illness. By August 31, contaminated lettuce had caused the largest outbreak of explosive diarrhea ever in the United States, with 12,883 cases reported across 21 states. By the time the CDC declared the outbreak over on September 11, some 570 people had been hospitalized and two had died. Another 8,113 cyclosporiasis infections have not been traced back to any source. “[This] was one of those events where you felt like the cracks showed,” Handy says.
paras.zh: 六月，密歇根州发现了第一例食源性疾病病例。截至 8 月 31 日，受污染的生菜已引发美国有史以来最大规模的爆发性腹泻疫情，21 个州报告了 12,883 例病例。截至 9 月 11 日 CDC 宣布疫情结束时，已有约 570 人住院治疗，其中两人死亡。另有 8,113 例环孢子虫病感染尚未追踪到任何来源。 “[这]是那些你感觉裂缝显现出来的事件之一，”汉迪说。

paras.en: But it isn’t easy to track the origins of foodborne illness. Typically, local and state public health officials report cases to the CDC — and investigate the outbreak, with the agency lending support as needed. If patient interviews reveal the culprit to be produce, dairy or packaged food, the CDC contacts the FDA, which identifies the producer and the distribution area — and coordinates recalls. The FDA also conducts on-the-ground investigations at the farms and processing facilities that supplied the food.
paras.zh: 但追踪食源性疾病的起源并不容易。通常，地方和州公共卫生官员向疾病预防控制中心报告病例，并调查疫情，该机构根据需要提供支持。如果对患者的访谈显示罪魁祸首是农产品、乳制品或包装食品，疾病预防控制中心会联系食品和药物管理局，由食品和药物管理局确定生产商和分销区域，并协调召回。 FDA 还对供应食品的农场和加工设施进行实地调查。

paras.en: It can take weeks to identify which contaminated foods are behind a foodborne illness outbreak. Each outbreak is different and timing can depend on the pathogen, laboratory evidence and availability of records, an FDA spokesperson told Science News. After Michigan health officials notified CDC that something was amiss on June 25, it was another 21 days before federal officials announced a possible culprit: shredded lettuce ultimately traced to a Taylor Farms processing facility in Mexico.
paras.zh: 确定哪些受污染的食品导致食源性疾病爆发可能需要数周时间。 FDA 发言人告诉《科学新闻》，每次爆发都是不同的，时间可能取决于病原体、实验室证据和记录的可用性。密歇根州卫生官员于 6 月 25 日通知 CDC 出现问题后，又过了 21 天，联邦官员才宣布可能的罪魁祸首：切碎的生菜最终追溯到墨西哥泰勒农场的一家加工厂。

paras.en: Of more than 20,000 cyclosporiasis cases reported this year, nearly 13,000 occurred across 21 states, with the preponderance of them in the Midwest.
paras.zh: 今年报告的 20,000 多例环孢子虫病病例中，近 13,000 例发生在 21 个州，其中大部分发生在中西部。

paras.en: The FDA aims to complete investigations as soon as possible. But delays in agency reporting early in the investigation led to unnecessary confusion about which foods to avoid in which states, said Sarah Sorscher, director of regulatory affairs at the Washington, D.C.–based Center for Science in the Public Interest, at a July 16 news briefing. “It’s a perfect storm for viral news. A lot of people have been posting on social media about avoiding fruits and vegetables, which is not good public health messaging.”
paras.zh: FDA 的目标是尽快完成调查。但华盛顿特区公共利益科学中心监管事务主任莎拉·索舍尔 (Sarah Sorscher) 在 7 月 16 日的新闻发布会上表示，调查初期机构报告的延迟导致了对哪些州应避免哪些食物产生不必要的混乱。 “这是一场病毒式新闻的完美风暴。很多人在社交媒体上发布了关于避免食用水果和蔬菜的帖子，这不是良好的公共卫生信息。”

paras.en: Sorscher applauded the dedication of public servants working to contain the outbreak. But she said they were working with inadequate support. “These programs are completely overwhelmed by the scale and scope of the work of solving and communicating these novel emerging outbreaks with a dwindling set of resources.”
paras.zh: 索舍尔对公务员为遏制疫情的奉献精神表示赞赏。但她表示，他们的工作支持不足。 “这些项目完全被用日益减少的资源来解决和传达这些新出现的疫情的工作的规模和范围所淹没。”

paras.en: Due in part to funding squeezes, in 2025 the CDC stopped mandatory surveillance of six foodborne pathogens, including the single-celled parasite that causes cyclosporiasis, Cyclospora. Speaking at the July 16 news briefing, epidemiologist Barbara Kowalcyk of George Washington University’s Institute for Food Safety and Nutrition Security in Washington, D.C., noted that half of CDC’s food safety budget goes to states to support surveillance and other programs. Yet that budget has remained flat for nearly a decade.
paras.zh: 部分由于资金紧张，疾病预防控制中心于 2025 年停止了对六种食源性病原体的强制监测，其中包括引起环孢子虫病的单细胞寄生虫环孢子虫。华盛顿特区乔治华盛顿大学食品安全和营养安全研究所的流行病学家芭芭拉·科瓦尔西克 (Barbara Kowalcyk) 在 7 月 16 日的新闻发布会上发表讲话时指出，CDC 食品安全预算的一半用于各州支持监测和其他项目。然而，该预算近十年来一直保持不变。

paras.en: FDA investigations have also been impacted, with foreign food inspections at historical lows. In the case of cyclosporiasis, delays gathering testing supplies and getting clearance from the Mexican government meant it took nearly a month for FDA investigators to arrive in Mexico once the source of the outbreak was identified, according to the New York Times. Once there, inspectors found the parasite in a wastewater tank at a Taylor Farms processing plant — and in a drainage ditch at a farm that supplied the lettuce. Since Cyclospora infects only humans, the probable contaminant was sewage from a source that has yet to be identified.
paras.zh: FDA的调查也受到影响，国外食品检查量处于历史低位。据《纽约时报》报道，就环孢子虫病而言，由于延误了收集检测用品和获得墨西哥政府许可的时间，这意味着 FDA 调查人员在确定疫情来源后花了近一个月的时间才抵达墨西哥。到达那里后，检查人员在泰勒农场加工厂的废水池和供应生菜的农场的排水沟中发现了寄生虫。由于环孢子虫仅感染人类，因此可能的污染物是来自尚未确定来源的污水。

paras.en: Without knowing the source of the contamination, it’s hard to know how to stop the parasite from reaching produce in the future, says Francisco Diez-Gonzalez, a food microbiologist at the University of Georgia in Athens. “It leaves us with the feeling that we most likely are going to have something similar next year.”
paras.zh: 雅典佐治亚大学食品微生物学家弗朗西斯科·迪兹·冈萨雷斯说，在不知道污染源的情况下，很难知道如何阻止寄生虫在未来接触农产品。 “这让我们感觉明年很可能会出现类似的情况。”

paras.en: Starting in 2027, FDA plans to increase surveillance of produce historically associated with Cyclospora and boost laboratory capacity in Mexico to speed up investigations.
paras.zh: 从 2027 年开始，FDA 计划加强对历史上与环孢子虫有关的农产品的监测，并提高墨西哥的实验室能力以加快调查速度。

paras.en: Outbreaks of other foodborne pathogens — including Salmonella, Listeria and E. coli — have popped up this year, but not at a rate that’s out of the ordinary, says Diez-Gonzalez, who served on the U.S. National Advisory Committee on Microbiological Criteria for Foods before the Trump administration disbanded it in 2025. That suggests the sky isn’t falling, though he and others are concerned about our future ability to quickly contain outbreaks.
paras.zh: 迪兹-冈萨雷斯曾在特朗普政府于 2025 年解散美国国家食品微生物标准咨询委员会之前任职，他表示，今年其他食源性病原体（包括沙门氏菌、李斯特菌和大肠杆菌）的爆发也有所爆发，但速度并没有异常。这表明天不会塌下来，尽管他和其他人对我们未来快速遏制疫情的能力感到担忧。

paras.en: “We may see [fewer] cases, but it’s not that they are disappearing,” Diez-Gonzalez says. “We will not be able to detect them because we don’t have the resources.”
paras.zh: “我们可能会看到[更少的]病例，但这并不是说它们正在消失，”迪兹-冈萨雷斯说。 “我们将无法检测到它们，因为我们没有资源。”

paras.en: When the WHO announced in May that an Ebola outbreak had erupted in the Democratic Republic of Congo, the virus had been simmering for months. People in the mining town of Mongbwalu, where the outbreak was first detected, began falling ill in January or earlier, according to reporting from Science. Armed conflict in the region has made the outbreak response difficult, says the WHO, and some aid workers and health facilities have been attacked.
paras.zh: 当世界卫生组织五月宣布刚果民主共和国爆发埃博拉疫情时，该病毒已酝酿数月之久。据《科学》杂志报道，首次发现疫情的采矿小镇蒙布瓦鲁 (Mongbwalu) 的人们在一月份或更早开始患病。世界卫生组织表示，该地区的武装冲突使疫情应对变得困难，一些援助人员和卫生设施遭到袭击。

paras.en: Confirmed Ebola cases as of November 15, 2026. To date, 5,593 people have died, and 3,109 have recovered
paras.zh: 截至2026年11月15日确诊的埃博拉病例。迄今为止，已有5,593人死亡，3,109人康复

paras.en: As cases and death counts soared in May, health officials scrambled to test a backlog of patient samples for Bundibugyo virus, the species behind what has become the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak ever recorded. As of November 15, there were 11,432 confirmed cases and 5,593 deaths. Roughly 3,109 people have recovered. Cases have also been detected in France, Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria.
paras.zh: 随着五月份病例和死亡人数飙升，卫生官员忙于对积压的患者样本进行本迪布焦病毒检测，这种病毒是有史以来增长最快的埃博拉疫情的幕后黑手。截至11月15日，确诊病例11432例，死亡5593例。大约有 3,109 人康复。法国、乌干达、肯尼亚和尼日利亚也发现了病例。

paras.en: Before the outbreak, the United States significantly scaled back international aid that once flowed from USAID and the CDC. Such cuts may have hampered Ebola monitoring before the outbreak was declared — and affected infection control measures such as contact tracing, says infectious disease physician Krutika Kuppalli of UT Southwestern Medical Center in Dallas.
paras.zh: 疫情爆发前，美国大幅削减了曾经来自美国国际开发署和疾病预防控制中心的国际援助。达拉斯德州大学西南医学中心的传染病医生克鲁蒂卡·库帕利 (Krutika Kuppalli) 表示，这种削减可能会阻碍埃博拉疫情爆发前的监测，并影响接触者追踪等感染控制措施。

paras.en: Kuppalli led an Ebola treatment unit in Sierra Leone during the 2014–2016 outbreak, the largest ever recorded. At the time, the CDC sent 1,450 physicians, epidemiologists and other experts to help out in affected areas. So far around 500 CDC employees stationed in the United States and abroad have responded to the current outbreak.
paras.zh: 2014 年至 2016 年埃博拉疫情爆发期间，库帕利在塞拉利昂领导了一个埃博拉治疗小组，这是有记录以来规模最大的一次。当时，疾病预防控制中心派出了1450名医生、流行病学家和其他专家前往受影响地区提供帮助。到目前为止，大约有 500 名 CDC 驻美国和国外的员工已经对当前的疫情做出了反应。

paras.en: By September, the U.S. State Department pledged $887 million toward the purchase of personal protective equipment and the building of new Ebola treatment units. That’s roughly a third of the total amount sent during the 2014–2016 outbreak. Still, earlier investments in public health could have saved lives and helped minimize transmission, Kuppalli says.
paras.zh: 截至 9 月，美国国务院承诺提供 8.87 亿美元用于购买个人防护设备和建造新的埃博拉治疗装置。这大约是 2014-2016 年疫情爆发期间发送总量的三分之一。库帕利说，尽管如此，早期对公共卫生的投资本来可以挽救生命并有助于最大限度地减少传播。

paras.en: Information-sharing has also been a huge problem, Kuppalli says. Prior to the second Trump administration, U.S. health officials were in constant contact with WHO teams that shared information about cases and contact-tracing efforts. After the United States withdrew from the WHO in January 2025, CDC officials had to coordinate with other groups such as UNICEF, the United Nations Children’s Fund.
paras.zh: 库帕利说，信息共享也是一个大问题。在特朗普第二届政府之前，美国卫生官员一直与世卫组织团队保持联系，分享有关病例和接触者追踪工作的信息。 2025年1月美国退出世界卫生组织后，疾控中心官员不得不与联合国儿童基金会、联合国儿童基金会等其他组织进行协调。

paras.en: Nevertheless, there has been some progress toward developing treatments and vaccines. Researchers in Congo are testing whether antivirals and engineered antibodies can stave off severe disease and death in people infected with Bundibugyo virus, and whether those treatments can protect people after exposure. In October, a large clinical trial began testing a vaccine that is already approved against the species that caused the 2014–2016 outbreak. Kuppalli and colleagues argued in September in the Lancet Infectious Diseases that the vaccine’s potential for cross-protection merited its use in high-risk situations.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，在开发治疗方法和疫苗方面还是取得了一些进展。刚果的研究人员正在测试抗病毒药物和工程抗体是否可以避免本迪布焦病毒感染者的严重疾病和死亡，以及这些治疗方法是否可以在暴露后保护人们。 10 月，一项大型临床试验开始测试一种疫苗，该疫苗已被批准用于对抗导致 2014-2016 年疫情爆发的物种。库帕利和同事在 9 月份的《柳叶刀传染病》杂志上指出，该疫苗具有交叉保护的潜力，值得在高风险情况下使用。

paras.en: Two Bundibugyo-specific vaccines are poised to join the new trial after early evidence in animals and people showed the shots are safe — and suggested they may be protective.
paras.zh: 动物和人类的早期证据表明注射疫苗是安全的，并表明它们可能具有保护作用，因此两种本迪布焦特定疫苗准备加入新试验。

paras.en: Conditions have improved in some parts of Congo, according to the WHO. But there are still hundreds of new cases per week, and other countries should be prepared to respond quickly if the virus crosses borders. “The longer this outbreak continues, the more opportunities the virus has to reach new communities,” Kuppalli says.
paras.zh: 据世界卫生组织称，刚果部分地区的情况有所改善。但每周仍有数百例新病例，其他国家应该做好准备，在病毒跨境时迅速做出反应。库帕利说：“疫情持续的时间越长，病毒传播到新社区的机会就越多。”

paras.en: The M.V. Hondius was in for a rough voyage the moment it set off from Ushuaia, Argentina, on April 1. A passenger on the small ship had contracted Andes hantavirus, a rodent-borne disease that can cause severe respiratory illness and death. By the time the outbreak was contained, 13 people were infected and three people had died. Public health experts say a lagging U.S. response let other countries take the lead — and suggests the country is not prepared for future epidemics.
paras.zh: MV 4月1日，洪迪斯号从阿根廷乌斯怀亚出发时，航行就遭遇了艰难。这艘小船上的一名乘客感染了安第斯汉坦病毒，这是一种啮齿动物传播的疾病，可导致严重的呼吸道疾病和死亡。到疫情得到控制时，已有 13 人感染，3 人死亡。公共卫生专家表示，美国的滞后反应让其他国家发挥了带头作用，并表明该国没有为未来的流行病做好准备。

paras.en: It’s unclear how the first patient, who died on April 11, was infected. Another patient died on the ship, and a third — who was allowed to board a plane — died in South Africa.
paras.zh: 目前尚不清楚第一例于 4 月 11 日死亡的患者是如何被感染的。另一名患者在船上死亡，第三名患者（获准登机）在南非死亡。

paras.en: More than 300 high-risk contacts, including people who spent more than 15 minutes with an infected individual, were quarantined and monitored across 33 countries and territories. None of them got sick. Nor did another 336 low-risk contacts who had brief encounters with someone who fell ill, and who monitored themselves for symptoms.
paras.zh: 33 个国家和地区的 300 多名高风险接触者，包括与感染者相处超过 15 分钟的人，均被隔离和监测。他们都没有生病。另外 336 名与患病者有过短暂接触并监测自己症状的低风险接触者也没有出现这种情况。

paras.en: The United States’ severed relationship with the WHO “in many ways hampered the [country’s] hantavirus outbreak response,” says Benjamin, of the American Public Health Association. Before 2025, U.S. experts frequently received information about emerging health threats from the organization. But confusion over who government officials could talk to likely resulted in knowledge gaps and communication delays, Benjamin says. “CDC was not engaged as early on as they needed to be on that outbreak.”
paras.zh: 美国公共卫生协会的本杰明表示，美国与世界卫生组织断绝的关系“在很多方面阻碍了该国对汉坦病毒疫情的应对”。 2025年之前，美国专家经常从该组织收到有关新出现的健康威胁的信息。但本杰明说，对政府官员可以与谁交谈的困惑可能会导致知识差距和沟通延误。 “疾病预防控制中心没有按照他们需要的那样尽早参与疫情爆发。”

paras.en: Instead, other countries including Spain, South Africa, Argentina and Chile played leading roles. After scientists in South Africa determined that Andes hantavirus was behind the outbreak on May 2, passengers disembarked in mid-May in Tenerife, Spain, where health officials screened for symptoms and helped people travel home.
paras.zh: 相反，西班牙、南非、阿根廷和智利等其他国家发挥了主导作用。南非科学家于 5 月 2 日确定安第斯山脉汉坦病毒是此次疫情爆发的幕后黑手，乘客于 5 月中旬在西班牙特内里费岛下船，当地卫生官员对症状进行筛查并帮助人们回家。

paras.en: The CDC didn’t set up a response team until after May 2, according to the New York Times. And controversy erupted over uneven U.S. quarantine practices, with some people forced to remain for weeks in quarantine units in Omaha, Neb., while others remained at home. “There was nothing standard” about the protocols, Osterholm says. “Almost everybody got a different approach.”
paras.zh: 据《纽约时报》报道，CDC 直到 5 月 2 日之后才成立应对小组。美国隔离措施的不均衡引发了争议，一些人被迫在内布拉斯加州奥马哈的隔离设施中停留数周，而另一些人则留在家里。奥斯特霍尔姆说，这些协议“没有任何标准”。 “几乎每个人都有不同的方法。”

paras.en: The outbreak, which ended July 2, was quickly contained in part because Andes hantavirus isn’t very contagious. Of more than 50 known hantaviruses, Andes hantavirus is the only one known to spread from person to person. Although some rare superspreaders transmit the virus to others through casual contact, transmission typically happens through close contact, such as spending long periods of time together or kissing. It would have been harder to stop a pathogen that spreads easily through the air, Osterholm says. “By the time that they recognized what was going on, transmission would have already occurred.”
paras.zh: 疫情于 7 月 2 日结束，很快就得到了遏制，部分原因是安第斯山脉汉坦病毒的传染性不强。在 50 多种已知的汉坦病毒中，安第斯山脉汉坦病毒是唯一已知可在人与人之间传播的病毒。尽管一些罕见的超级传播者通过偶然接触将病毒传播给他人，但传播通常是通过密切接触发生的，例如长时间在一起或接吻。奥斯特霍尔姆说，阻止很容易通过空气传播的病原体会更加困难。 “当他们意识到发生了什么时，传播已经发生了。”

paras.en: The international collaboration had some successes, says virologist Gustavo Palacios of the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai in New York City. Experts in South Africa “kept digging when everything was negative,” he says, until they finally identified Andes hantavirus as the cause.
paras.zh: 纽约市西奈山伊坎医学院的病毒学家古斯塔沃·帕拉西奥斯表示，国际合作取得了一些成功。他说，南非的专家“在一切都呈阴性的情况下继续挖掘”，直到他们最终确定安第斯汉坦病毒是病因。

paras.en: Hantavirus infections are also relatively rare in the Americas, for now. Studies suggest climate change will increase the likelihood that hantaviruses — and other zoonotic illnesses like Ebola — will make the jump from animals to humans. Dense cities can make it easier for diseases to spread. And such threats don’t disappear when funding for studying them dries up.
paras.zh: 目前，汉坦病毒感染在美洲也相对罕见。研究表明，气候变化将增加汉坦病毒以及埃博拉等其他人畜共患疾病从动物传播到人类的可能性。密集的城市会使疾病更容易传播。当研究这些威胁的资金枯竭时，这些威胁也不会消失。

paras.en: “The strongest lesson [from the M.V. Hondius] is that outbreak response depends on the knowledge and the relationships that already exist before the event,” Palacios says. Of the billions of viruses on Earth, just a few hundred pose threats to people. With enough resources, researchers can work together to learn as much as possible about those pathogens and be better prepared when a new one emerges — just as previous work on coronaviruses made the rollout of COVID-19 vaccines possible within a year of the pandemic’s start.
paras.zh: “（来自 M.V. Hondius 的）最深刻的教训是，疫情应对取决于事件发生前已经存在的知识和关系，”帕拉西奥斯说。在地球上数十亿种病毒中，只有几百种对人类构成威胁。有了足够的资源，研究人员就可以共同努力，尽可能多地了解这些病原体，并在新病原体出现时做好更好的准备——就像之前对冠状病毒的研究使得在大流行开始一年内推出 COVID-19 疫苗成为可能。

paras.en: “We will not always know in advance which [pathogens] will become important,” Palacios says. But by not tracking rare threats that could one day become larger problems, “we are shooting ourselves in the foot.”
paras.zh: “我们并不总是能提前知道哪些[病原体]会变得重要，”帕拉西奥斯说。但如果不追踪有朝一日可能成为更大问题的罕见威胁，“我们就是在搬起石头砸自己的脚。”

articles.title: Two stars in the Andromeda galaxy merged before astronomers’ eyes
articles.author: Meghan Bartels

paras.en: For seven years, a giant star in the Andromeda galaxy grew brighter. It swelled to more than twice its original size, even as its surface temperature barely changed. Then, in October 2025, it erupted. The slow brightening and sudden eruption tell a story of a smaller star orbiting inside of a massive star and what became of the pair, researchers report November 18 in Nature.
paras.zh: 七年来，仙女座星系中的一颗巨星变得越来越亮。尽管其表面温度几乎没有变化，但它膨胀到原来大小的两倍多。然后，2025年10月，它爆发了。研究人员于 11 月 18 日在《自然》杂志上报道，缓慢的变亮和突然的喷发讲述了一颗较小的恒星在一颗大质量恒星内部运行的故事，以及这对恒星后来的演变。

paras.en: In work published last year, after poring through nearly 30 years of telescope data, astronomers had found that the giant began brightening in 2018 and proposed that a smaller star was circling ever closer around a giant companion and had even slipped inside its outermost layers. Astronomers call this elusive phase of a binary star’s life common-envelope evolution.
paras.zh: 在去年发表的研究中，天文学家在仔细研究了近 30 年的望远镜数据后发现，这颗巨星在 2018 年开始变亮，并提出一颗较小的恒星正在围绕一颗巨大的伴星旋转得越来越近，甚至滑入了它的最外层。天文学家将双星生命中这个难以捉摸的阶段称为共包层演化。

paras.en: Now, the astronomers have analyzed the system’s dramatic next developments, culminating in the October 2025 eruption. (The stars are nicknamed Little Bao and Big Bao as a nod to that event’s official designation, AT 2025abao.)
paras.zh: 现在，天文学家已经分析了该系统接下来的戏剧性发展，最终导致 2025 年 10 月的喷发。 （这些明星被昵称为“小包”和“大包”，以纪念该赛事的官方名称 AT 2025abao。）

paras.en: First, astrophysicist Viraj Karambelkar of Columbia University and colleagues revisited those years of brightening given the imminent eruption. One cause of the brightening could have been gas flowing away from the stars, giving off light as it slowed down. But even if all the energy of that moving gas turned into light, it still wouldn’t be enough to explain the glow.
paras.zh: 首先，哥伦比亚大学的天体物理学家维拉吉·卡拉姆贝尔卡（Viraj Karambelkar）及其同事在即将爆发的情况下重新审视了那些年的明亮现象。变亮的原因之一可能是气体从恒星流走，在减速时发出光。但即使移动气体的所有能量都转化为光，仍然不足以解释这种发光。

paras.en: Instead, the researchers determined that the binary hypothesis they had originally proposed fit better: As Little Bao orbited inside Big Bao’s gas outer layers, the gas pushed back against the little star. That drag made Little Bao spiral inward and transfer energy to the surrounding gas. Some of that energy escaped as light, making Big Bao shine brighter.
paras.zh: 相反，研究人员认为他们最初提出的二元假设更适合：当小包在大包的气体外层内绕轨道运行时，气体向后推小恒星。那股阻力让小宝向内盘旋，将能量传递给周围的气体。一些能量以光的形式逸出，使大包变得更加明亮。

paras.en: Then, it was time to dig into what caused the eruption. If the outburst threw enough of the shared gas into space, the individual stars could have survived in an even tighter orbit. But the team estimates that only about a tenth of the giant’s outer gas escaped. The energy carried by that fast-moving gas also suggests that Little Bao reached Big Bao’s core. Together, those clues point to a merger.
paras.zh: 然后，是时候深入研究导致火山喷发的原因了。如果爆发将足够多的共享气体抛入太空，那么单个恒星就可以在更紧密的轨道上幸存下来。但研究小组估计，只有大约十分之一的巨人外部气体逸出。那种快速移动的气体所携带的能量也表明小包到达了大包的核心。所有这些线索都指向合并。

paras.en: Still, too much dust clouds the system to directly see what remains. And it won’t settle for years or even decades, although Karambelkar and his colleagues will be watching.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，太多的灰尘覆盖了系统，无法直接看到剩下的东西。尽管卡拉姆贝尔卡和他的同事们会密切关注，但这种情况在几年甚至几十年内都不会解决。

paras.en: They’ll be looking for more examples of this type of merger, too. “Now we can go and try to look for similar systems,” Karambelkar says, “and hopefully aim to catch more of these systems even before they erupt.”
paras.zh: 他们还将寻找更多此类合并的例子。卡拉姆贝尔卡说：“现在我们可以尝试寻找类似的系统，并希望能够在更多的系统爆发之前捕获它们。”

articles.title: New discovery reveals what may be holding back room-temperature superconductors

paras.en: New discovery reveals what may be holding back room-temperature superconductors
paras.zh: 新发现揭示了可能阻碍室温超导体发展的因素

paras.en: - Utrecht University, Faculty of Science
paras.zh: - 乌得勒支大学理学院

paras.en: - A major breakthrough in superconductivity research has revealed that one of the essential ingredients for electricity to flow without resistance can exist at room temperature. Scientists discovered that electrons can form stable pairs at much higher temperatures than previously understood, suggesting that a different obstacle may be preventing room-temperature superconductivity.
paras.zh: - 超导研究的一项重大突破表明，电流无阻力流动的基本成分之一可以在室温下存在。科学家发现，电子可以在比之前理解的温度高得多的温度下形成稳定的电子对，这表明可能有另一个障碍阻碍了室温超导性。

paras.en: Imagine trains floating above their tracks, energy storage systems that waste almost no electricity, and quantum computers operating with extraordinary efficiency. Superconductivity could help make these technologies possible, but a major challenge has stood in the way for more than a century. Most superconducting materials function only when cooled to extremely low temperatures, making widespread use costly and complicated.
paras.zh: 想象一下漂浮在轨道上方的火车、几乎不浪费电力的储能系统以及以非凡效率运行的量子计算机。超导可以帮助使这些技术成为可能，但一个多世纪以来，一个重大挑战一直困扰着我们。大多数超导材料只有在冷却到极低温度时才能发挥作用，这使得广泛使用成本高昂且复杂。

paras.en: Now, researchers from Utrecht, Leiden, and Munich have uncovered an important clue about how superconductivity might eventually work at room temperature. Their findings, published in the journal Science, reveal that one of the essential requirements for superconductivity can already be satisfied without extreme cooling. The discovery offers a promising new direction in the search for materials that conduct electricity without resistance.
paras.zh: 现在，来自乌得勒支、莱顿和慕尼黑的研究人员发现了关于超导最终如何在室温下发挥作用的重要线索。他们的研究结果发表在《科学》杂志上，表明超导的基本要求之一已经可以在不极度冷却的情况下得到满足。这一发现为寻找无电阻导电材料提供了一个有前景的新方向。

paras.en: To understand why this matters, consider something as ordinary as a toaster. When electricity passes through its metal heating element, electrical resistance causes the wire to heat up and glow red, producing the heat needed to toast bread.
paras.zh: 要理解为什么这很重要，请考虑像烤面包机这样普通的东西。当电流通过其金属加热元件时，电阻使电线升温并发出红光，产生烤面包所需的热量。

paras.en: That resistance is useful for cooking, but in most electrical systems, it creates unwanted energy losses. Even something as simple as charging a phone involves some electricity being converted into heat rather than being put to useful work.
paras.zh: 这种电阻对于烹饪很有用，但在大多数电气系统中，它会产生不必要的能量损失。即使是像给手机充电这样简单的事情，也会将一些电能转化为热量，而不是用于有用的工作。

paras.en: Why Superconductivity Requires Extreme Cold
paras.zh: 为什么超导需要极冷

paras.en: Superconductivity eliminates this problem by allowing electrical current to move through certain materials with zero resistance. In principle, this could dramatically improve the efficiency of electrical systems and enable technologies that are difficult or expensive to operate today.
paras.zh: 超导允许电流以零电阻穿过某些材料，从而消除了这个问题。原则上，这可以显着提高电气系统的效率，并实现当今操作困难或昂贵的技术。

paras.en: The challenge is temperature. Many superconductors must be cooled to approximately -260°C using liquid helium before they exhibit this remarkable behavior. Maintaining such extreme conditions requires substantial energy and expensive cooling equipment, limiting practical applications.
paras.zh: 挑战是温度。许多超导体必须使用液氦冷却至约 -260°C，才能表现出这种非凡的行为。维持这种极端条件需要大量能源和昂贵的冷却设备，限制了实际应用。

paras.en: Superconductivity was first observed in 1911. Decades later, in the mid-1980s, researchers discovered a new class of materials that could become superconducting at much warmer temperatures, around -173°C. Although still extremely cold, this represented an important advance.
paras.zh: 超导现象首次在 1911 年被观测到。几十年后，在 20 世纪 80 年代中期，研究人员发现了一类新型材料，可以在更高的温度（约 -173°C）下实现超导。尽管仍然非常寒冷，但这代表了一个重要的进步。

paras.en: However, these materials introduced a major scientific mystery. The established theory that successfully describes conventional, low-temperature superconductivity could not explain how the newer materials worked. Despite decades of research, the mechanisms behind high-temperature superconductivity remain poorly understood.
paras.zh: 然而，这些材料带来了一个重大的科学谜团。成功描述传统低温超导性的既定理论无法解释新型材料的工作原理。尽管经过了数十年的研究，高温超导背后的机制仍然知之甚少。

paras.en: "We don't understand superconductivity at these higher temperatures at all," says Ingmar Swart [LINK], one of the research leaders. "And if you don't understand it, you can't systematically search for materials that become superconducting at room temperature, which is ultimately our goal."
paras.zh: 研究负责人之一英格玛·斯瓦特 (Ingmar Swart) [LINK] 表示：“我们根本不了解高温下的超导性。” “如果你不理解它，你就无法系统地寻找在室温下成为超导的材料，而这正是我们的最终目标。”

paras.en: A Crucial Ingredient Works at Room Temperature
paras.zh: 一种在室温下发挥作用的关键成分

paras.en: The new study provides an important piece of the puzzle. Swart and his colleagues have demonstrated that one of the two fundamental conditions needed for superconductivity can exist even at room temperature.
paras.zh: 这项新研究提供了这个难题的重要组成部分。斯瓦特和他的同事已经证明，超导所需的两个基本条件之一即使在室温下也可以存在。

paras.en: "This is really good news," says Swart. "We show that one of the two key conditions for superconductivity can be met at room temperature. If that weren't possible, room-temperature superconductivity would be out of reach altogether."
paras.zh: “这确实是个好消息，”斯沃特说。 “我们表明，超导的两个关键条件之一可以在室温下满足。如果不可能，那么室温超导将完全无法实现。”

paras.en: The finding suggests that scientists may need to focus less on whether electrons can form the necessary connections and more on how those electrons coordinate their behavior.
paras.zh: 这一发现表明，科学家可能需要更少关注电子是否能够形成必要的连接，而更多地关注这些电子如何协调它们的行为。

paras.en: The Secret Lies in How Electrons Move Together
paras.zh: 秘密在于电子如何一起移动

paras.en: Superconductivity depends on two essential processes. First, electrons must join together in pairs called Cooper pairs. Second, those pairs must move in a coordinated way, maintaining a shared quantum state that allows electrical current to flow without resistance.
paras.zh: 超导性取决于两个基本过程。首先，电子必须成对地结合在一起，称为库珀对。其次，这些对必须以协调的方式移动，保持共享的量子态，使电流能够无阻力地流动。

paras.en: An analogy is a dance floor filled with ten couples. Having each couple dance together is only the first step. For the entire group to move as one, all ten couples must also coordinate their movements.
paras.zh: 打个比方，舞池里挤满了十对情侣。让每对情侣一起跳舞只是第一步。为了让整个团队作为一个整体移动，所有十对情侣也必须协调他们的动作。

paras.en: In conventional superconductors, electron pairing and this collective coordination emerge at the same temperature. The new findings show that high-temperature superconductors behave differently. Their electrons can form pairs at temperatures substantially higher than those needed for superconductivity itself to appear.
paras.zh: 在传统的超导体中，电子配对和这种集体配位在相同的温度下出现。新发现表明高温超导体的行为有所不同。它们的电子可以在远高于超导本身出现所需温度的温度下形成对。

paras.en: Even more remarkably, the researchers found that these pairs can remain intact at room temperature.
paras.zh: 更值得注意的是，研究人员发现这些对在室温下可以保持完整。

paras.en: "The 'glue' that holds the pairs together is strong enough to keep them together even at room temperature," says Swart. "This suggests that the second key ingredient, phase coherence, is the bottleneck."
paras.zh: “将这些对粘合在一起的‘胶水’足够坚固，即使在室温下也能将它们粘合在一起，”斯瓦特说。 “这表明第二个关键因素，即相位一致性，是瓶颈。”

paras.en: Phase coherence describes the coordinated quantum behavior of the electron pairs. Without it, the pairs may exist, but the material does not become superconducting. This suggests that achieving and maintaining that coordination could be the crucial remaining challenge.
paras.zh: 相位相干性描述了电子对的协调量子行为。没有它，电子对可能存在，但材料不会变成超导。这表明实现和维持这种协调可能是剩下的关键挑战。

paras.en: "If we understand phase coherence, it may point to a path toward superconductivity at higher temperatures."
paras.zh: “如果我们理解相位相干性，它可能会指出一条在更高温度下实现超导的道路。”

paras.en: Swart intends to investigate this process in future research, with the goal of understanding how superconductivity might be sustained at increasingly warmer temperatures.
paras.zh: 斯沃特打算在未来的研究中调查这一过程，目的是了解超导性如何在日益升高的温度下维持。

paras.en: New Technology Reveals a Hidden Superconductivity Clue
paras.zh: 新技术揭示了隐藏的超导线索

paras.en: The breakthrough was made possible by specialized measurement equipment designed and constructed by the research team.
paras.zh: 这一突破是由研究团队设计和建造的专门测量设备实现的。

paras.en: Unlike conventional measurement approaches, the new instruments could distinguish electrical current flowing through individual electrons from current carried by paired electrons. This allowed the researchers to examine when electron pairs formed and how they behaved inside the material.
paras.zh: 与传统的测量方法不同，新仪器可以区分流经单个电子的电流和成对电子携带的电流。这使得研究人员能够检查电子对何时形成以及它们在材料内的行为方式。

paras.en: By separating these two contributions, the team gained a clearer picture of the processes underlying high-temperature superconductivity and identified where a critical obstacle may lie.
paras.zh: 通过区分这两个贡献，该团队对高温超导性的过程有了更清晰的了解，并确定了可能存在的关键障碍。

paras.en: The findings do not mean that room-temperature superconductivity has been achieved. They do, however, demonstrate that one of its essential ingredients can survive under everyday temperature conditions. Understanding how to make those electron pairs act together could bring scientists closer to a long-sought breakthrough in electrical technology.
paras.zh: 这些发现并不意味着室温超导已经实现。然而，他们确实证明了其基本成分之一可以在日常温度条件下生存。了解如何使这些电子对共同作用可以让科学家们更接近长期以来寻求的电气技术突破。

paras.en: Materials provided by Utrecht University, Faculty of Science. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由乌得勒支大学理学院提供。注意：内容的风格和长度可能会被编辑。

paras.en: - Jiasen Niu, Maialen Ortego Larrazabal, Thomas Gozlinski, Yudai Sato, Koen M. Bastiaans, Tjerk Benschop, Jian-Feng Ge, Yaroslav M. Blanter, Genda Gu, Ingmar Swart, Milan P. Allan. paras.zh: - Jiasen Niu、Maialen Ortego Larrazabal、Thomas Gozlinski、Yudai Sato、Koen M. Bastiaans、Tjerk Benschop、Jian-Feng Ge、Yaroslav M. Blanter、Genda Gu、Ingmar Swart、Milan P. Allan。铜酸盐高温超导体中赝能隙和配对能的等效性。科学，2026； 394 (6824): 682 DOI: 10.1126/science.adt3444

articles.title: Scientists create a remarkable new rechargeable battery using vitamin B12

paras.en: Scientists create a remarkable new rechargeable battery using vitamin B12
paras.zh: 科学家利用维生素 B12 创造出一种非凡的新型可充电电池

paras.en: - Scientists have found a surprising new use for vitamin B12, developing a rechargeable battery that uses the essential nutrient to help generate and store electricity. The prototype survived up to 250 charging cycles and could open the door to safer, cheaper, and more environmentally friendly alternatives to lithium-ion batteries.
paras.zh: - 科学家们发现了维生素 B12 的惊人新用途，即开发一种可充电电池，利用这种必需营养素来帮助发电和储存电力。该原型机可承受高达 250 次充电周期，为更安全、更便宜、更环保的锂离子电池替代品打开了大门。

paras.en: Scientists have found an unexpected new use for vitamin B12, a nutrient best known for its importance to human health. Researchers at the University of Córdoba have incorporated the vitamin into a rechargeable battery, demonstrating for the first time that it can serve as a catalyst in this type of energy storage system.
paras.zh: 科学家们发现了维生素 B12 的一种意想不到的新用途，这种营养素因其对人类健康的重要性而闻名。科尔多瓦大学的研究人员将这种维生素融入可充电电池中，首次证明它可以作为此类能量存储系统的催化剂。

paras.en: Vitamin B12 is essential for normal bodily function and is naturally present in animal products. The vitamin is produced by certain bacteria, which occur in nature and are also grown commercially to supply the food and pharmaceutical industries. In addition to its established applications in medicine, nutrition, and veterinary care, B12 is used to address certain nutritional deficiencies. It has also become popular alongside other B vitamins as a hangover remedy because of its potential to help reduce fatigue.
paras.zh: 维生素 B12 对于正常的身体功能至关重要，天然存在于动物产品中。这种维生素是由某些细菌产生的，这些细菌存在于自然界中，也可以进行商业种植以供应食品和制药行业。除了在医学、营养和兽医护理方面的既定应用外，B12 还用于解决某些营养缺乏症。它还与其他 B 族维生素一起作为解酒药物而广受欢迎，因为它有可能有助于减轻疲劳。

paras.en: Now, scientists are exploring an entirely different application. By using the vitamin to support the chemical reactions inside a battery, they have developed a prototype capable of completing up to 250 charging and discharging cycles.
paras.zh: 现在，科学家们正在探索一种完全不同的应用。通过使用维生素来支持电池内部的化学反应，他们开发了一种能够完成多达 250 次充电和放电循环的原型。

paras.en: How Vitamin B12 Makes a Rechargeable Battery Possible
paras.zh: 维生素 B12 如何使可充电电池成为可能

paras.en: The new battery was developed by the Physical Chemistry research group (FQM-204) at the University of Córdoba's Chemical Institute for Energy and the Environment (IQUEMA). It uses zinc and oxygen from the surrounding air to produce electricity, with vitamin B12, also called cobalamin, playing a crucial role in the process.
paras.zh: 这种新型电池是由科尔多瓦大学能源与环境化学研究所（IQUEMA）的物理化学研究小组（FQM-204）开发的。它利用周围空气中的锌和氧气来发电，维生素 B12（也称为钴胺素）在此过程中发挥着至关重要的作用。

paras.en: To make the design work, the researchers attached vitamin B12 molecules to single-walled carbon nanotubes. The vitamin contains cobalt (III) at its center, which helps drive the electrochemical reactions needed for the battery to function.
paras.zh: 为了使设计发挥作用，研究人员将维生素 B12 分子附着在单壁碳纳米管上。这种维生素的中心含有钴 (III)，有助于驱动电池发挥作用所需的电化学反应。

paras.en: The team has previously experimented with natural molecules as battery catalysts, including hemoglobin and catalase. These substances contain iron (II) and iron (III), respectively. Vitamin B12 represents the group's third effort to use a biological molecule for this purpose, but it has delivered an important advance: a battery that can be recharged repeatedly, completing as many as 250 cycles.
paras.zh: 该团队此前曾尝试使用天然分子作为电池催化剂，包括血红蛋白和过氧化氢酶。这些物质分别含有铁（II）和铁（III）。维生素 B12 代表了该小组利用生物分子实现这一目的的第三次努力，但它带来了一个重要的进步：一种可以反复充电、完成多达 250 个循环的电池。

paras.en: One of the biggest obstacles was keeping vitamin B12 inside the battery. Because the vitamin dissolves readily in water, it would normally be difficult to retain in a system that relies on a water-based electrolyte.
paras.zh: 最大的障碍之一是将维生素 B12 保留在电池内。由于维生素很容易溶解在水中，因此通常很难保留在依赖水基电解质的系统中。

paras.en: The researchers overcame this problem by securing the vitamin to carbon nanotubes, using an approach inspired by how amino acids connect to form proteins.
paras.zh: 研究人员通过将维生素固定在碳纳米管上克服了这个问题，采用的方法受到氨基酸如何连接形成蛋白质的启发。

paras.en: Manuel Cano Luna, one of the study's authors, explained that "we looked at the properties we can find in naturally occurring materials to use them in new batteries," while describing the team's search for useful biological compounds.
paras.zh: 该研究的作者之一曼努埃尔·卡诺·卢纳 (Manuel Cano Luna) 解释说，“我们研究了天然材料的特性，以便将它们用于新电池”，同时描述了该团队对有用生物化合物的探索。

paras.en: Their attachment technique imitates "the process by which amino acids bind together in proteins."
paras.zh: 他们的附着技术模仿了“蛋白质中氨基酸结合在一起的过程”。

paras.en: Alongside Cano Luna, the research team included Valentín García Caballero, Miguel López León, Pablo Gómez Argudo, Luis Camacho Delgado, José Miguel Rodríguez Mellado, María Teresa Martín Romero, José Abad López, and Antonio Jesús Fernández Romero.
paras.zh: 除了 Cano Luna 之外，研究团队还包括 Valentín García Caballero、Miguel López León、Pablo Gómez Argudo、Luis Camacho Delgado、José Miguel Rodríguez Mellado、María Teresa Martín Romero、José Abad López 和 Antonio Jesús Fernández Romero。

paras.en: A Safer, Lighter Alternative to Lithium-Ion Batteries
paras.zh: 更安全、更轻的锂离子电池替代品

paras.en: The findings, published in the Journal of Materials Chemistry A, could contribute to the development of battery technologies that depend less on the materials used in conventional lithium-ion batteries.
paras.zh: 该研究结果发表在《材料化学杂志 A》上，可能有助于减少对传统锂离子电池所用材料的依赖的电池技术的发展。

paras.en: Although lithium-ion batteries are widely used, obtaining their raw materials can involve significant economic, environmental, and social challenges. Zinc-air batteries offer a potential alternative because they can store substantial amounts of energy relative to their weight while relying on materials that are more readily available.
paras.zh: 尽管锂离子电池被广泛使用，但获取其原材料可能会带来重大的经济、环境和社会挑战。锌空气电池提供了一种潜在的替代方案，因为它们可以存储相对于其重量的大量能量，同时依赖更容易获得的材料。

paras.en: Zinc is abundant and recyclable, and these batteries use oxygen from the surrounding atmosphere as part of their energy-producing reactions. Because they draw oxygen from the air rather than storing all the necessary reactants internally, they can also be lighter than other battery designs.
paras.zh: 锌含量丰富且可回收，这些电池使用周围大气中的氧气作为其能量产生反应的一部分。由于它们从空气中吸取氧气，而不是在内部存储所有必要的反应物，因此它们也比其他电池设计更轻。

paras.en: This advantage has helped make zinc-air batteries increasingly useful in compact electronic devices, particularly hearing aids. Another benefit is their use of non-flammable, water-based electrolytes, which can reduce fire risks and improve safety.
paras.zh: 这一优势使得锌空气电池在紧凑型电子设备（尤其是助听器）中越来越有用。另一个好处是它们使用不易燃的水基电解质，可以降低火灾风险并提高安全性。

paras.en: A major challenge in developing rechargeable zinc-air batteries is finding a catalyst that can efficiently support the chemical reactions involved in both producing and storing electricity.
paras.zh: 开发可充电锌空气电池的一个主要挑战是找到一种能够有效支持发电和储存电力所涉及的化学反应的催化剂。

paras.en: During discharge, the battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy. Recharging requires the relevant chemical reactions to proceed in the opposite direction. A suitable catalyst must therefore be effective in both processes.
paras.zh: 在放电过程中，电池将化学能转化为电能。充电需要相关的化学反应向相反的方向进行。因此，合适的催化剂必须对这两个过程都有效。

paras.en: According to researcher Antonio Jesús Fernández Romero, vitamin B12 "has proven to meet the necessary conditions to act as a good catalyst because, during discharge, it catalyzes the reduction of oxygen to water and, during recharging, it promotes the production of oxygen."
paras.zh: 研究人员 Antonio Jesús Fernández Romero 表示，维生素 B12“已被证明满足作为良好催化剂的必要条件，因为在放电过程中，它会催化氧气还原成水，而在充电过程中，它会促进氧气的产生。”

paras.en: This ability to support both reactions is what makes the vitamin particularly promising for rechargeable zinc-air battery technology.
paras.zh: 这种支持这两种反应的能力使得维生素在可充电锌空气电池技术中特别有前景。

paras.en: Could Vitamin B12 Help Store Renewable Energy?
paras.zh: 维生素 B12 可以帮助储存可再生能源吗？

paras.en: The successful prototype offers a new direction for researchers seeking affordable, sustainable alternatives to existing energy storage technologies.
paras.zh: 这个成功的原型为研究人员寻求经济实惠、可持续的现有储能技术替代方案提供了新的方向。

paras.en: If the approach can be developed further, batteries using vitamin B12 catalysts could eventually help address one of the biggest challenges facing renewable energy: storing excess electricity generated by sources such as solar and wind power for use when production falls.
paras.zh: 如果这种方法能够进一步发展，使用维生素 B12 催化剂的电池最终可以帮助解决可再生能源面临的最大挑战之一：储存太阳能和风能等来源产生的多余电力，以在产量下降时使用。

paras.en: Although the technology remains at the research stage, demonstrating up to 250 charge and discharge cycles shows that a familiar biological molecule can play an unexpected role in rechargeable battery design. The discovery adds to growing efforts to use naturally occurring substances to create safer, lighter, and more sustainable ways to store energy.
paras.zh: 尽管该技术仍处于研究阶段，但最多 250 次充电和放电循环的演示表明，熟悉的生物分子可以在可充电电池设计中发挥意想不到的作用。这一发现进一步推动了利用天然物质创造更安全、更轻、更可持续的能源储存方式的努力。
